body: ## Motivation https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/20021784695/job/57446087825 Our AMD CI workflow always pulls the latest pre-built daily Docker image and then installs dependencies based on the PR code. However, this installation step does not rebuild or update AITER, which is already baked into the pre-built image. As a result, when a PR upgrades the AITER version, the CI does not actually test against the new AITER, but instead tests against whatever version was pre-built into the daily image. This leads to a blind spot where AITER-related regressions cannot be caught at PR time. **Example**: In the PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14497 , we upgraded AITER to v0.1.7.post5. In our later manual tests we found that this version introduces an accuracy regression in: accuracy-test-2-gpu-amd (linux-mi325-gpu-2) However, the CI for this PR incorrectly passed(see in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/20021784695/job/57446087825), because it was still using the older AITER version bundled in the daily image, not the upgraded version specified in the PR. **Conclusion:** We need CI to verify whether the AITER version in the PR matches the one inside the pulled image. If they differ, CI must rebuild/install the correct AITER version inside the container before running tests. cc: @bingxche @michael-amd @saienduri ## Modifications ## Accuracy Tests #### Simulation - aiter version upgraded to v0.1.8 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/20368597241/job/58529505129 #### Simulation - If aiter version unchanged https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/20388611486/job/58594282444?pr=15460 ## Benchmarking and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). - [x] Work with maintainers to merge your PR. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process)

author: gaurav7261
body:
## Why I'm doing:
[BugFix] Fix SIGSEGV in Int32ToDateConverter for NULL values on ARM64                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                
    The Int32ToDateConverter::convert() method was unconditionally accessing                                                                                                                        
    src_data[i] for all rows, including NULL values. When Parquet statistics                                                                                                                        
    contain NULL dates (common in Delta Lake tables with deletion vectors),                                                                                                                         
    the underlying data array is uninitialized, causing SIGSEGV when accessed.                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    Reproduction case:                                                                                                                                                                              
    - Delta Lake table with DATE column                                                                                                                                                             
    - Query with date predicate: WHERE day > current_date - interval 1 day                                                                                                                          
    - Parquet row group statistics contain NULL min/max                                                                                                                                             
    - Zone map filtering calls Int32ToDateConverter::convert()                                                                                                                                      
    - Crash at: dst_data[i]._julian = src_data[i] + UNIX_EPOCH_JULIAN                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                   
   This crash was architecture-specific (ARM64/Graviton) because:                                                                                                                                  
    - ARM has stricter memory access patterns than x86_64                                                                                                                                           
    - Uninitialized memory contains different bit patterns on ARM                                                                                                                                   
    - x86_64 had the same latent bug but often didn't crash                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    Root cause:                                                                                                                                                                                     
    - resize_uninitialized() uses RawAllocator (no initialization for performance)                                                                                                                  
    - append_nulls() sets null flag but leaves data uninitialized                                                                                                                                   
    - Int32ToDateConverter accessed uninitialized data for NULL rows                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                    
     

## What I'm doing:

Fixes #issue

Fix: Add null check before accessing data, consistent with other                                                                                                                                
    converters (Int32ToTimeConverter, Int32ToDateTimeConverter).                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    Changes:                                                                                                                                                                                        
    - Add null flag check: if (!src_null_data[i])                                                                                                                                                   
    - Only convert non-null date values                                                                                                                                                             
    - Replace memcpy with loop for consistency                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                    
    Fixes: SIGSEGV during Parquet zone map filtering with NULL date statistics                                                                                                                      
    Tested: ARM64 (Graviton) and x86_64

body:
## Summary

Establishes a precise baseline of the current Attributes Settings + Edit behavior and identifies the root cause of the "blank until resave" issue.

## Root Cause Identified ✅

**Schema mismatch between legacy and canonical attribute documents:**

| Schema | Field Name | Example Attribute |
|--------|------------|-------------------|
| Canonical | `data_type` | `age_group` |
| Legacy | `dataType` | `rics_source.brand` |

When the frontend form expects `data_type` but receives `dataType`, it falls back to defaults, showing blank fields.

### Why Resave Fixes It

The UPDATE handler runs Zod validation which applies schema defaults:
1. GET returns raw Firestore data (no normalization)
2. UPDATE merges patch → validates with Zod → writes normalized data
3. After resave, document has canonical field names

## Summary
Implements the final step (Step 4) of the setup wizard - the summary page where users review their configuration before completing setup.

## Changes
- **Shadcn Tooltip**: Installed and integrated tooltip component
- **Summary Display**: Shows account email, n8n instance details, and workflow count
- **Interactive Tooltip**: Hover over workflow count to see list of selected workflow names
- **API Integration**: Fetches workflow names and calls  on finish
- **Typography**: Matches exact Figma specs (14px medium labels, 16px regular values)
- **Layout**: Same 546px container pattern as other setup pages
- **UX**: Loading states for workflow fetching and completion process

## Design
Fully matches Figma design at https://www.figma.com/design/7uj8oIQE74SyFsUsrThl3T/elova--%3E-Onboarding?node-id=130-1213

## Features
- ✅ Displays setup data from context (account, instance, workflows)
- ✅ Fetches workflow names to show in tooltip
- ✅ Shadcn tooltip showing workflow names on hover
- ✅ Complete button with loading state
- ✅ Calls  with all setup data
- ✅ Redirects to dashboard on success
- ✅ Error handling with user feedback

## Testing
Tested the complete setup flow:
1. Account creation
2. n8n connection
3. Workflow selection
4. Summary review → All data displays correctly
5. Complete button → Calls API successfully

author: jm-rivera
body:
This pull request updates the World Bank data importer to improve cache reliability and observability. It ensures that the cache's write-ahead log (WAL) is properly persisted across sessions by closing the cache on process exit, and adds logging to indicate when data is loaded from cache. The version is also bumped to 0.4.2.

@lpicci96 FYI

**World Bank cache reliability and observability:**
* Ensured the World Bank data cache is properly closed on process exit using `atexit.register(_DATA_CACHE.close)`, which persists the WAL and fixes cache not persisting across sessions.
* Enabled cache hit/miss statistics tracking with `_DATA_CACHE.stats(enable=True)` and added logging to indicate when data is loaded from cache in `get_data`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d685e8966375061a2429d3f3f44601cb7010846135e0138f4bf5b7468708ab1dR40-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d685e8966375061a2429d3f3f44601cb7010846135e0138f4bf5b7468708ab1dR540) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d685e8966375061a2429d3f3f44601cb7010846135e0138f4bf5b7468708ab1dR554-R557)

**Documentation and versioning:**
* Updated the changelog to document the cache persistence fix and cache hit logging.
* Bumped project version to 0.4.2 in `pyproject.toml`.

**Code maintenance:**
* Added `import atexit` to support proper cache cleanup.

author: stephanedelcroix
body:
## Summary

This PR adds **Procrastinate**, a fun anti-productivity app that demonstrates several advanced .NET MAUI features including **MEAI (Microsoft.Extensions.AI)** integration.

## MEAI Features Demonstrated

- **IChatClient** — On-device AI via `AppleIntelligenceChatClient` (iOS/macOS)
- **IChatClient** — Cloud AI via OpenAI-compatible adapter (Groq/Llama)
- **IEmbeddingGenerator** — `NLEmbeddingGenerator` for quality scoring of generated excuses
- **Multi-Agent Pipeline** — 3-agent chain (Researcher→Writer→Editor) with reasoning panel
- **BYOM (Bring Your Own Model)** — Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, etc.)
- **Embedded ONNX Model** — In-process `OnnxRuntimeGenAI` with HuggingFace model download
- **Hybrid AI Switching** — Settings UI to switch between local/cloud/pipeline/custom/embedded modes

## Other Features Demonstrated

- **Shell Navigation** — Tab-based navigation with 5 main pages
- **Localization** — Full translation in 7 languages (English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, Czech, Ukrainian)
- **Custom Theming** — Nord color palette with dark/light theme support
- **Mini-Games** — 9 games including TicTacToe with AI opponent (via IChatClient)
- **XAML Source Generator** — Uses `MauiXamlInflator=SourceGen`
- **Plugin.Maui.Audio** — Sound effects for Simon Says game
- **SecureStorage** — API keys stored securely (Keychain/EncryptedSharedPrefs)

## Hackday Challenge Levels Covered

- 🟢 **Basic**: Local AI via AppleIntelligenceChatClient + cloud AI via Groq
- 🟡 **Advanced**: Hybrid model switching, NLEmbedding quality scoring, BYOM endpoints
- 🟠 **Agent Framework**: 3-agent pipeline with reasoning display
- 🔴 **Freestyle**: Embedded ONNX model (Phi-3 Mini) running entirely on-device

## Original Repository

https://github.com/StephaneDelcroix/procrastinate

## Testing

```bash
# iOS (requires .NET 10 SDK + dotnet10 nightly feed)
dotnet build -f net10.0-ios

# Android
dotnet build -f net10.0-android

# macOS
dotnet build -f net10.0-maccatalyst
```

author: copilot
body:
Build a GPS navigation device to guide hikers back to their starting position using ESP32-S3 with Waveshare 1.47" LCD, HGLRC M100-5883 M10 GPS module, and HMC5883L compass.

## Implementation

**Core Navigation**
- GPS coordinate tracking with TinyGPS++ parsing NMEA sentences
- Compass heading from HMC5883L magnetometer via I2C
- Haversine formula for distance calculation (meters/km)
- Great circle bearing computation with proper angle normalization (-180° to +180°)
- Persistent home position storage in flash memory (Preferences API)

**Display & UI**
- 172x320 ST7789 LCD with color-coded status indicators
- Visual arrow overlay pointing toward home (relative to current heading)
- Non-blocking feedback system using state machine (replaced blocking `delay()`)
- Real-time updates: GPS lock status, satellite count, coordinates, heading, distance, bearing

**Hardware Interface**
- UART1 (GPIO 17/18) for GPS communication at 9600 baud
- I2C (GPIO 8/9) for compass at 3.3V
- SPI display on built-in Waveshare pins
- BOOT button (GPIO 0) triggers home position save

## Code Structure

```cpp
// Non-blocking home save feedback
if (showHomeSavedFeedback) {
  if (currentTime - homeSavedFeedbackTime < HOME_SAVED_FEEDBACK_DURATION) {
    // Show green confirmation screen
    return; // Skip normal display update
  }
  showHomeSavedFeedback = false;
}

// Arrow angle normalization handles wraparound
float relativeAngle = bearingToHome - heading;
while (relativeAngle > 180.0) relativeAngle -= 360.0;
while (relativeAngle < -180.0) relativeAngle += 360.0;
drawCompassArrow(COMPASS_CENTER_X, COMPASS_CENTER_Y, COMPASS_RADIUS, relativeAngle);
```

## Documentation

- Hardware setup with pinouts and BOM (~$50-85)
- Step-by-step usage instructions for field navigation
- ASCII wiring schematic
- Troubleshooting guide covering GPS lock, compass calibration, display issues
- Quick reference card for printing
- Safety disclaimers emphasizing device is navigation aid, not replacement for map/compass skills

## Dependencies

PlatformIO project targeting `esp32-s3-devkitc-1` with libraries:
- TinyGPSPlus (GPS parsing)
- Adafruit GFX + ST7789 (display)
- Adafruit HMC5883 Unified (compass)
- Adafruit BusIO + Unified Sensor (I2C abstraction)

## 🚀 Release Summary
This release merges significant improvements to the core `axion-hdl` logic, GUI, and test infrastructure. Key highlights include "Smart Persistence" for safe file regeneration, a completely refactored test suite that ensures repository cleanliness, and major updates to the web-based GUI editor.

## ✨ Key Features & Improvements

### 1. 🧠 Smart Persistence & Core Logic
- **Intelligent Overwrite**: The generator now intelligently handles existing files, preserving manual modifications where possible unless `Overwrite` is forced.
- **Enhanced Parsing**: Improved robustness for [yaml](cci:1://file:///Users/bugratufan/Desktop/git/axion-hdl/tests/run_tests.py:1613:0-1659:18), [json](cci:1://file:///Users/bugratufan/Desktop/git/axion-hdl/tests/run_tests.py:1662:0-1708:18), and [xml](cci:7://file:///Users/bugratufan/Desktop/git/axion-hdl/output/spi_controller_regs.xml:0:0-0:0) inputs, including better handling of comments and wide signals.
- **Conflict Detection**: Granular address conflict reporting and overlap detection.

### 2. 🧪 Test Suite Refactoring
- **Zero Pollution**: Refactored [run_tests.py](cci:7://file:///Users/bugratufan/Desktop/git/axion-hdl/tests/run_tests.py:0:0-0:0) to use a global temporary directory for all test generation. No more generated files left in `tests/vhdl` or `output`.
- **CI Stability**: Fixed hardcoded paths in C tests and simulation processing that were causing CI failures.
- **Coverage**: All **249 tests** are passing.

### 3. 🎨 GUI Enhancements
- **Editor Upgrades**: New "Diff View" for inspecting changes before saving.
- **Activity Log**: Real-time feedback for configuration refreshes.
- **Visual Polish**: Improved responsiveness and error reporting in the web interface.

### 4. 📚 Documentation
- Consolidated documentation structure (`docs/source`).
- New guides for "Requirements", "Rule Checker", and "Examples".

## ✅ Verification
- **Tests**: `make test` passing (249/249).
- **Cleanliness**: Verified that the repository remains clean after full test execution.

Deep Scan synthesis data was being generated but UI sections rendered empty when data was missing or incomplete, leaving users without feedback on analysis status. ## Changes ### UI Fallback Messages - Modified all render functions (`renderExecutiveSummary`, `renderPageAnalyses`, `renderJourneyMap`, `renderActionPlan`, `renderRoadmap`) to display informative messages when data is unavailable instead of hiding panels - Fixed conditional rendering to always show deep scan sections for deep scans, even when in-progress ```javascript // Before: panel hidden when no data if (!summary || summary.length === 0) { if (panel) panel.style.display = 'none'; return; } // After: panel shown with fallback message if (panel) panel.style.display = 'block'; if (!summary || summary.length === 0) { container.innerHTML = '

Deep analysis not generated yet...

'; return; } ``` ### JSON Extraction & Error Handling - Added `_extract_json_from_text()` helper to handle OpenAI responses wrapped in markdown/text - Enhanced error handling to store raw response on parse failure for debugging - Applied to both `synthesize_deep_scan()` and `analyze_single_page()` ### Database Schema - Added missing `what_to_fix_first` column to `scan_summaries` table via migration - Updated INSERT and SELECT queries to include the field - Fixed API response serialization in both `/api/scan/{id}` endpoints ### AI Prompt Enhancement - Added explicit minimum requirements to synthesis prompt (5 summary bullets, 3+ journey steps) - Prevents empty synthesis outputs from AI ### Code Quality - Extracted magic number to `DEEP_SCAN_RAW_RESPONSE_LIMIT` constant - Removed duplicate `DEEP_SCAN_TEXT_SAMPLE_LIMIT` definition All changes confined to `api.py` with surgical edits to minimize risk.
Original prompt > TASK: Deep Scan report is missing depth. Summary + page-by-page sections render empty. Fix end-to-end. > > Find where deep scan analysis is generated (OpenAI call) and where results are saved into the scan record (SQLite). author: trash0101
body:
This PR updates the TypeScript definitions to more accurately reflect Tabulator’s runtime behavior.

Validator typing:
- Allows passing a validator directly as a function ` (cell, value) => boolean`
- While the docs primarily show custom validators wrapped in an object (`{ type, parameters }`), the documentation explicitly states that “you can pass a function to the validator property”, which implies direct function support. This change aligns the typings with that documented intent and existing usage.
https://tabulator.info/docs/6.3/validate#func-custom

EditorParams typing:
- Replaces `{}` with `Record<string, unknown>` for editor parameter objects
- `{}` allows non-object values and prevents safe property access, which breaks valid usage
- `object` is too weak for configuration objects and disallows property access entirely
- `any` would be overly permissive for a public types package

https://tabulator.info/docs/6.3/edit#overview

Although the README recommends avoiding `Object`-like types, `Record<string, unknown>` is used here to model “an object with arbitrary keys” while still preventing primitives and preserving type safety. The actual shape of editor params is editor-specific and user-defined, so a more specific object type is not possible in this case.

author: luisfabib
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive global configuration system for FHIRcraft, enabling users to control validation behavior both globally and within specific code blocks. The main changes include the addition of a new configuration module, integration of configuration options into the validation logic, and extensive documentation and top-level API exposure for configuration management.

### Added

- Added a new `fhircraft/config.py` module that defines `ValidationConfig` and `FHIRCraftConfig` dataclasses, provides thread-safe global and context-local configuration management, and exposes functions for configuring, resetting, and modifying validation settings. This includes context manager support and environment variable loading.
- Added a new user guide section (`docs/user-guide/configuration.md`) detailing configuration options, usage patterns, environment variable support, best practices, and practical examples for the new configuration system.

### Changed

- Updated `_validate_FHIR_element_constraint` in `fhircraft/fhir/resources/validators.py` to respect the new configuration system, allowing validation to be globally or selectively disabled, errors to be converted to warnings, and constraints to be enabled/disabled dynamically. Towards #146

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR optimizes the HTTP connection pool in `pkg/upstream/http`. Previously, the pool created a new `http.Client` (and thus a new `http.Transport` and connection pool) for every item in the generic pool. This meant that connections could not be reused across different "clients" in the pool, leading to high connection churn and defeating the purpose of HTTP keep-alives in a high-concurrency scenario.

The change hoists the `http.Client` creation and TLS configuration outside the pool factory. All pooled items now wrap the same `http.Client` instance, allowing them to share the underlying `http.Transport` and its idle connections. `MaxIdleConns` and `MaxIdleConnsPerHost` are updated to match the pool's `maxSize` to ensure the transport can hold enough idle connections for the concurrency level.

This also eliminates redundant I/O (certificate reading) and parsing during pool expansion.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR optimizes the `Sidebar` component to prevent unnecessary re-renders during video playback and transcript editing.

**Problem:**
The `Sidebar` component consumes `ProcessContext` via `useProcessContext()`. This context contains `currentTime`, which updates up to 60 times per second during playback. Even though `Sidebar` itself does not use `currentTime` in its main render loop (only passing it implicitly to children or not using it at all), the context update triggers a full re-render of the `Sidebar` component function, regenerating the Virtual DOM tree for the entire sidebar structure (tabs, headers, containers).

**Solution:**
We wrapped the returned JSX of `Sidebar` in `useMemo`. The dependency array includes all variables used in the JSX (e.g., `selectedJob`, `activeSidebarTab`, `STYLE_PRESETS`, handlers) but **explicitly excludes** `currentTime`.
This ensures that when `currentTime` updates:
1. The `Sidebar` function still runs (due to context hook).
2. `useMemo` compares dependencies. Since `currentTime` is not a dependency and other deps are stable, it returns the *cached* JSX object.
3. React sees the same JSX object reference and skips reconciliation for the `Sidebar`'s children (except those that consume context themselves, like `TranscriptPanel`).

**Changes:**
- Modified `frontend/src/features/process/components/Sidebar.tsx` to wrap the return block in `useMemo`.
- Moved the `if (!selectedJob) return null;` check inside the `useMemo` callback to comply with Rules of Hooks (hooks must be called unconditionally).
- Verified that all event handlers used in dependencies are stable (already wrapped in `useCallback`).

**Verification:**
- `pnpm lint` passed (no new warnings, confirmed dependencies are exhaustive).
- `pnpm test SidebarTabs` passed (functionality preserved).

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [sqlparse](https://pypi.org/project/sqlparse) from **0.4.2** to **0.5.5**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 0.5.5
   ```
   ----------------------------

Bug Fixes

* Fix DoS protection to raise SQLParseError instead of silently returning None
  when grouping limits are exceeded (issue827).
* Fix splitting of BEGIN TRANSACTION statements (issue826).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.5.4
   ```
   ----------------------------

Enhancements

* Add support for Python 3.14.
* Add type annotations to top-level API functions and include py.typed marker
  for PEP 561 compliance, enabling type checking with mypy and other tools
  (issue756).
* Add pre-commit hook support. sqlparse can now be used as a pre-commit hook
  to automatically format SQL files. The CLI now supports multiple files and
  an `--in-place` flag for in-place editing (issue537).
* Add `ATTACH` and `DETACH` to PostgreSQL keywords (pr808).
* Add `INTERSECT` to close keywords in WHERE clause (pr820).
* Support `REGEXP BINARY` comparison operator (pr817).

Bug Fixes

* Add additional protection against denial of service attacks when parsing
  very large lists of tuples. This enhances the existing recursion protections
  with configurable limits for token processing to prevent DoS through
  algorithmic complexity attacks. The new limits (MAX_GROUPING_DEPTH=100,
  MAX_GROUPING_TOKENS=10000) can be adjusted or disabled (by setting to None)
  if needed for legitimate large SQL statements.
* Remove shebang from cli.py and remove executable flag (pr818).
* Fix strip_comments not removing all comments when input contains only
  comments (issue801, pr803 by stropysh).
* Fix splitting statements with IF EXISTS/IF NOT EXISTS inside BEGIN...END
  blocks (issue812).
* Fix splitting on semicolons inside BEGIN...END blocks (issue809).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.5.3
   ```
   ----------------------------

Bug Fixes

* This version introduces a more generalized handling of potential denial of
  service attack (DOS) due to recursion errors for deeply nested statements.
  Brought up and fixed by living180. Thanks a lot!
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.5.2
   ```
   ----------------------------

Bug Fixes

* EXTENSION is now recognized as a keyword (issue785).
* SQL hints are not removed when removing comments (issue262, by skryzh).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.5.1
   ```
   ----------------------------

Enhancements

* New "compact" option for formatter. If set, the formatter tries to produce
  a more compact output by avoiding some line breaks (issue783).

Bug Fixes

* The strip comments filter was a bit greedy and removed too much
  whitespace (issue772).
  Note: In some cases you might want to add `strip_whitespace=True` where you
  previously used just `strip_comments=True`. `strip_comments` did some of the
  work that `strip_whitespace` should do.
* Fix error when splitting statements that contain multiple CASE clauses
  within a BEGIN block (issue784).
* Fix whitespace removal with nested expressions (issue782).
* Fix parsing and formatting of ORDER clauses containing NULLS FIRST or
  NULLS LAST (issue532).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.5.0
   ```
   ----------------------------

Notable Changes

* Drop support for Python 3.5, 3.6, and 3.7.
* Python 3.12 is now supported (pr725, by hugovk).
* IMPORTANT: Fixes a potential denial of service attack (DOS) due to recursion
  error for deeply nested statements. Instead of recursion error a generic
  SQLParseError is raised. See the security advisory for details:
  https://github.com/andialbrecht/sqlparse/security/advisories/GHSA-2m57-hf25-phgg
  The vulnerability was discovered by uriyay-jfrog. Thanks for reporting!

Enhancements

* Splitting statements now allows to remove the semicolon at the end.
  Some database backends love statements without semicolon (issue742).
* Support TypedLiterals in get_parameters (pr749, by Khrol).
* Improve splitting of Transact SQL when using GO keyword (issue762).
* Support for some JSON operators (issue682).
* Improve formatting of statements containing JSON operators (issue542).
* Support for BigQuery and Snowflake keywords (pr699, by griffatrasgo).
* Support parsing of OVER clause (issue701, pr768 by r33s3n6).

Bug Fixes

* Ignore dunder attributes when creating Tokens (issue672).
* Allow operators to precede dollar-quoted strings (issue763).
* Fix parsing of nested order clauses (issue745, pr746 by john-bodley).
* Thread-safe initialization of Lexer class (issue730).
* Classify TRUNCATE as DDL and GRANT/REVOKE as DCL keywords (based on pr719
  by josuc1, thanks for bringing this up!).
* Fix parsing of PRIMARY KEY (issue740).

Other

* Optimize performance of matching function (pr799, by admachainz).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.4.4
   ```
   ----------------------------

Notable Changes

* IMPORTANT: This release fixes a security vulnerability in the
  parser where a regular expression vulnerable to ReDOS (Regular
  Expression Denial of Service) was used. See the security advisory
  for details: https://github.com/andialbrecht/sqlparse/security/advisories/GHSA-rrm6-wvj7-cwh2
  The vulnerability was discovered by erik-krogh from GitHub
  Security Lab (GHSL). Thanks for reporting!

Bug Fixes

* Revert a change from 0.4.0 that changed IN to be a comparison (issue694).
  The primary expectation is that IN is treated as a keyword and not as a
  comparison operator. That also follows the definition of reserved keywords
  for the major SQL syntax definitions.
* Fix regular expressions for string parsing.

Other

* sqlparse now uses pyproject.toml instead of setup.cfg (issue685).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.4.3
   ```
   ----------------------------

Enhancements

* Add support for DIV operator (pr664, by chezou).
* Add support for additional SPARK keywords (pr643, by mrmasterplan).
* Avoid tokens copy (pr622, by living180).
* Add REGEXP as a comparision (pr647, by PeterSandwich).
* Add DISTINCTROW keyword for MS Access (issue677).
* Improve parsing of CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (pr662, by chezou).

Bug Fixes

* Fix spelling of INDICATOR keyword (pr653, by ptld).
* Fix formatting error in EXTRACT function (issue562, issue670, pr676, by ecederstrand).
* Fix bad parsing of create table statements that use lower case (issue217, pr642, by mrmasterplan).
* Handle backtick as valid quote char (issue628, pr629, by codenamelxl).
* Allow any unicode character as valid identifier name (issue641).

Other

* Update github actions to test on Python 3.10 as well (pr661, by cclaus).
   ```
   
  
</details>


 

<details>
  <summary>Links</summary>
  
  - PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/sqlparse
  - Changelog: https://data.safetycli.com/changelogs/sqlparse/
</details>

This pull request migrates the `apps/fishing-map` project from using Jest to Vitest for unit testing and introduces Playwright for end-to-end (E2E) testing. It updates related configuration files, scripts, and dependencies, and adds initial test utilities and E2E test examples. Additionally, it makes some minor code and import path improvements.

**Testing Infrastructure Migration and Improvements**

* Replaces Jest with Vitest for unit testing:
  - Removes `jest.config.ts` and `tsconfig.spec.json` files, and updates `tsconfig.json` to reference Vitest types and change `moduleResolution` to `bundler`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ad1e1f13218b7c9eccccc0582151ed50b0c8214ed2edc04280b792e04b7a2f58L1-L14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-eb38338ee2391bb1d208abb1da41dc2b344cc20372fbcb87686a34b04546502aL1-L16) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c03efc7519ae5427f84baf368b8cb3a20930e91e0a9b91abe0e447e73de35899L8-R15) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c03efc7519ae5427f84baf368b8cb3a20930e91e0a9b91abe0e447e73de35899L19-R26)
  - Adds `vitest.config.mts` with browser and coverage support, and updates `project.json` to run Vitest for the `test` target. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-08b45b4fdf285068858ffa56e8e9df85962b8a241d4d96c2e67280c0a57bf3bbR1-R70) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7a10fb32d4c98e68458fafd263ba05b99bb5dd02ade00a8df6398aa6fdde8e08L134-R149)
  - Adds test utilities in `test/appTestUtils.tsx` for rendering with Redux and simulating guest users.
  - Adds a sample Vitest test for `UserSection`.
  - Updates `package.json` scripts to use Vitest.

* Adds Playwright for E2E testing:
  - Adds Playwright configuration (`playwright.config.mts`) and a sample E2E test for login/logout flow. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-466730df9796155353928ee591bd52ab3d6df35f53bd035d7eb854a090aa158bR1-R78) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f41633708da0854e2671176d10b0cbdd1a26fc28faa23c14b1d562c2ca32c9f8R1-R29)
  - Adds a `test-e2e` target in `project.json` and corresponding script in `package.json`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7a10fb32d4c98e68458fafd263ba05b99bb5dd02ade00a8df6398aa6fdde8e08L134-R149) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5161107bd2e1c036df7f544c071ad85753d707d99eb3fcaffa33c956625a87beL15-R17)
  - Updates `tsconfig.json` to include Playwright and related types.

* Updates Nx and related dependencies to latest versions, including adding `@nx/vitest` and `@playwright/test`.
* Updates Nx configuration to support Vitest caching and removes old Jest/Vite test cache entries. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-15552e50b1b7c05b05b7ffe08ee47b5ed62b8d2039229c58972a42fd22a7381cL64-L67) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-15552e50b1b7c05b05b7ffe08ee47b5ed62b8d2039229c58972a42fd22a7381cR91-R94)
* Adds `migrations.json` for Nx migrations.

**Codebase and Configuration Cleanups**

* Updates `.nvmrc` to Node.js 24.12.0.
* Improves import paths for `UserSection` and related components for better structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f0b553e358e143e5120fd4f0cf0d51d570634cb0c45e7393f0e652a1175c7574L22-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3ed35170c778c05a0c0c8494e985d00b455c4fec16c569376b526870692b9cdfL34-R34) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0c048ac76b28472b62d8700841c7ac45d281fbd9c4a95202fa7685b1e03160c7L28-R29)
* Updates `i18next.config.ts` to ignore test files and directories during extraction.
* Minor prop renaming for test IDs (`data-test` → `data-testid`).
* Adds an empty `beforeEach` in `test/vitest.setup.ts` for future test setup.

These changes modernize the testing stack, improve test maintainability, and lay the groundwork for better test coverage and developer experience.

author: iovergaard
body:
## Summary
- Fixes issue where changing a property's variation setting (Shared/Invariant ↔ Variant) via Infinite Editing caused document save to fail with 404 error
- Adds value migration fallback logic to find values when culture/segment doesn't match exactly
- Overrides `reload()` to process incoming data through `_processIncomingData()` for proper value transformation

Fixes #21195

## Root Cause
When a property's variation setting was changed via Infinite Editing, the document's values in memory still had the old culture/segment format. The base class `reload()` method was fetching raw data without processing it through `_processIncomingData()`, which contains the value migration logic.

## Changes
1. **`property-value-preset-variant-builder.controller.ts`**: Added `#findExistingValue()` method with fallback logic:
   - Handles invariant → variant migration (uses null-culture value for all variants)
   - Handles variant → invariant migration (uses first culture value for invariant)

2. **`content-detail-workspace-base.ts`**: 
   - Added property variation cache and observer to detect changes
   - Override `reload()` to call `_processIncomingData()` for proper value transformation

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests pass (8 tests in variant builder controller)
- [x] Manual testing: Change property from Shared to Variant → Save document works
- [x] Manual testing: Change property from Variant to Shared → Save document works
- [x] Values are preserved during variation changes

body:
### Motivation
- Provide robust JSONL-safe log rotation for core and edge and ensure long-running JSONL writers are handled (`copytruncate`).
- Emit structured alerts on failures/thresholds so operators get actionable `alerts.jsonl` entries.
- Detect timer/service/disk problems and automatically quarantine/disable noisy edges to protect ingest.
- Make pull pipeline respect disabled edges to avoid repeatedly pulling from quarantined nodes.

### Description
- Added core and edge logrotate configs: `core/etc/logrotate.d/rockpix-core` and `edge/etc/logrotate.d/rockpix-edge` (JSONL-safe, `copytruncate`).
- New alert writer: `core/scripts/write_alert.py` (installs/execs as `rockpix-write-alert`) that appends structured JSONL alert rows.
- Healthcheck and size-guard tooling:
  - `core/scripts/ops_healthcheck.sh` + systemd unit/timer (`core/systemd/rockpix-ops-health.{service,timer}`) to check timers and disk free space and emit alerts.
  - `core/scripts/size_guard.sh` + systemd unit/timer (`core/systemd/rockpix-size-guard.{service,timer}`) to monitor ingest/edge file sizes, force `logrotate` when hard thresholds hit, mark quarantine and append disabled edges to `/etc/rockpix/edges.disabled`.
  - `edge/scripts/edge_size_guard.sh` for local edge-side size checks and local alerting + optional forced rotate.
- OnFailure handler: `core/systemd/rockpix-onfailure@.service` to emit alert when critical services fail.
- Pull script update: patched `core/scripts/pull_edges.sh` to skip edges listed in `DISABLED_FILE` (`/etc/rockpix/edges.disabled`) so quarantined/disabled edges are ignored.
- Set executables for relevant scripts (`write_alert.py`, `ops_healthcheck.sh`, `size_guard.sh`, `edge_size_guard.sh`) and added files to the repo.

### Testing
- Performed repository-level validations and housekeeping commands: `ls`/`sed` inspections, set executable bits (`chmod`), `git add` and `git commit` — these commands completed successfully.
- Verified `core/scripts/pull_edges.sh` was patched and is executable (`stat`/`git status` showed modifications staged/committed).
- No automated unit or integration tests were executed for systemd activation, `logrotate` runtime, or live alert delivery in this rollout.
- Recommend enabling the timers and running smoke tests on a staging host: `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl enable --now rockpix-size-guard.timer rockpix-ops-health.timer` and exercising `rockpix-write-alert` to confirm alerts land in `/var/log/rockpix/alerts/alerts.jsonl`.

author: mro68
body:
## Summary

The `location()` method in the OpenDAL backend now returns `opendal:{scheme}:{name}` instead of just `opendal:{name}`.

## Motivation

This change enables downstream code to identify which OpenDAL service is being used. For example:
- `opendal:gdrive:MyFolder` for Google Drive
- `opendal:s3:my-bucket` for S3

## Use Cases

- **Backend-specific optimizations**: e.g., PackCachingBackend for GDrive (see follow-up PR #445)
- **Better logging and debugging**: Clearly shows which backend type is in use
- **Consistent format**: Aligns with how other backends report their location

## Changes

- Modified `location()` in `crates/backend/src/opendal.rs` to include the scheme
- Updated doc comment to reflect the new format

## Related PRs

| PR | Repo | Description | Dependency |
|----|------|-------------|------------|
| #445 | rustic_core | PackCachingBackend (uses this for GDrive detection) | depends on this PR |
| [#7059](https://github.com/apache/opendal/pull/7059) | apache/opendal | GDrive batch listing optimization | independent, but complements |

## Note on OpenDAL Dependency

This PR is part of a larger effort to make Google Drive a viable backend for rustic. For **optimal GDrive performance**, the following OpenDAL PR should also be merged:

> **[apache/opendal#7059](https://github.com/apache/opendal/pull/7059)** - Implements batch recursive listing for GDrive (~50x faster directory listing)

This rustic_core PR works independently, but the full performance benefits (~45-50x speedup) are only realized when combined with the OpenDAL improvement.

## Summary
README.mdの更新に従い、以下の機能を実装しました：
- Purposeテーブルに`createdBy`フィールドを追加して、アンケート作成者を識別
- トップページで作成済みアンケート（自分が作成したもの）と回答済みアンケート（自分が回答したもの）を分けて表示
- 各セクションに適切なフィルタリングを適用

## Changes

### 1. Database Schema (`prisma/schema.prisma`)
- Purposeモデルに`createdBy: String`フィールドを追加
- `createdBy`にインデックスを追加してクエリを高速化
- デフォルト値`"unknown"`を設定（既存データ対応）
- マイグレーションを実行

### 2. API Updates

#### `src/app/api/purposes/route.ts`
- **GET**: `createdBy`クエリパラメータでフィルタリング可能に
- **POST**: `createdBy`を必須パラメータとして追加

#### `src/app/api/answered-surveys/route.ts` (新規作成)
- `clientId`でResponseテーブルを検索
- JOINしてPurpose情報を取得
- 重複を除去して回答済みアンケート一覧を返す

### 3. Frontend Updates

#### `src/app/edit/page.tsx`
- `getOrCreateClientId`をインポート
- Purpose保存時に`createdBy`として`clientId`を送信

#### `src/app/page.tsx`
- **作成済みアンケート**セクション:
  - `createdBy`パラメータで自分が作成したアンケートのみ取得
  - 共有URL、集計確認、自分の回答を編集ボタンを表示
- **回答済みアンケート**セクション（新規追加）:
  - `/api/answered-surveys`から自分が回答したアンケートを取得
  - 自分の回答を編集、集計確認ボタンを表示
- localStorageから`clientId`を取得して両方のセクションで使用

## Technical Details

### Data Flow
1. ユーザーがアンケートを作成
   - localStorage → `clientId`取得/生成
   - Purpose作成時に`createdBy = clientId`を設定
2. トップページ表示
   - localStorage → `clientId`取得
   - 作成済み: `GET /api/purposes?createdBy={clientId}`
   - 回答済み: `GET /api/answered-surveys?clientId={clientId}`
3. 結果を別々のセクションで表示

### Database Migration
```sql
ALTER TABLE "Purpose" ADD COLUMN "createdBy" TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown';
CREATE INDEX "Purpose_createdBy_idx" ON "Purpose"("createdBy");
```

## Test plan
- [ ] 新しいアンケートを作成し、トップページの「作成済みアンケート」に表示されることを確認
- [ ] 他のアンケートに回答し、トップページの「回答済みアンケート」に表示されることを確認
- [ ] 別のブラウザ/シークレットモードで同じアンケートに回答し、元のブラウザでは「回答済みアンケート」に表示されないことを確認
- [ ] localStorageをクリアして再読み込みし、どちらのセクションも空になることを確認
- [ ] 既存のデータ（createdBy="unknown"）が正常に動作することを確認

body:
Comprehensive Product Requirements Document for MonoGame Hub—a cross-platform desktop application for managing MonoGame projects, templates, and community content, with initial application implementation and fully functional core services.

## Documents Included

### Framework-Analysis.md
Detailed comparison of **12 modern cross-platform frameworks** including .NET native, Rust native, and web-based options:

**Top Tier (.NET Native):**
- **Avalonia UI** (93/100) - Recommended
- .NET MAUI (90/100) - Disqualified due to Linux limitations
- Uno Platform (86/100)

**Rust + Web Hybrid:**
- Tauri (74/100)

**Traditional Cross-Platform:**
- Flutter (71/100)

**Rust Native Frameworks:**
- Slint (68/100) - Declarative UI, tiny bundle size, but Rust-only
- iced (64/100) - Pure Rust reactive GUI, poor .NET integration
- egui (63/100) - Immediate mode for tools, not polished apps

**Web-Based Desktop:**
- Qt/PySide6 (66/100)
- React Native (62/100) - Experimental Linux support
- Neutralinojs (60/100)
- Electron (59/100)

Includes feature matrix, weighted scoring, pros/cons analysis, sentiment evaluation, and executive summary with recommendation. Rust frameworks offer excellent performance and tiny bundle sizes but require complex FFI/CLI wrappers for .NET operations. React Native fails the Linux requirement with experimental/incomplete desktop support.

### MonoGame-Hub-PRD.md
Complete technical specification and implementation roadmap.

## Technical Architecture
- **Framework**: Avalonia UI for native Windows/macOS/Linux support with single .NET codebase
- **Rationale**: Perfect .NET 10 integration, true cross-platform support including Linux, 93/100 score in comprehensive 12-framework analysis
- **Pattern**: MVVM with dependency injection, 7 core services (Project, Template, NuGet, Blog, Resource, IDE, Settings)
- **Stack**: .NET 10.0 (current latest), SQLite for local storage, Markdown.Avalonia for content rendering

## Core Features Specified

### Project Management
- Recursive folder scanning with platform detection (DesktopGL, WindowsDX, iOS, Android)
- Legacy MGCB vs modern Pipeline differentiation via `MonoGame.Content.Builder.Task` and `.mgcb` file presence
- Wildcard version resolution (e.g., `3.8.5-develop.*`) through NuGet registry queries
- Build/run/restore actions with IDE integration (VS, VS Code, Rider)

### Template Installation
- NuGet API integration for stable/preview/development release discovery
- Install/uninstall workflow with automatic cleanup: `dotnet new uninstall` → `dotnet new install <version>`
- Visual differentiation: pre-release templates highlighted in MonoGame Orange (#E73C00)

### Project Creation
- Wizard with template selection, automatic `dotnet new` execution
- Post-creation: `dotnet restore` + `dotnet tool restore` (legacy MGCB only)
- Optional Git initialization and IDE launch

### Settings & Environment
- NuGet cache folder configuration (updates `NUGET_PACKAGES` env var)
- Detected .NET SDK version display with download links for .NET 9/10/11
- IDE preference selection with platform-specific detection logic

### Community Integration
- Blog feed from https://monogame.net/blog/ with tag filtering and search
- Resources catalog from https://monogame.net/resources/ with category/tag filters
- In-app markdown rendering for post content

## UI/UX Design
- Six-tab interface: Projects, Installs, New Project, Settings, News, Resources
- Dark theme default with MonoGame Orange (#E73C00) accents
- ASCII mockups provided for all screens
- Unity Hub-inspired but distinct visual identity

## Implementation Roadmap
- 8 phases over 13 weeks: Foundation → Project Management → Templates → Creation → IDE Integration → Community → Polish → Beta
- Testing strategy covers unit/integration/UI tests with xUnit and Avalonia UI Testing
- Performance targets: <2s startup, <5s scanning 100 projects, 60 FPS UI

## Application Implementation

### MonoGame-Hub/ Application Structure
Created complete application structure with **Avalonia UI 11.3.10** and **.NET 10.0**:

**Projects:**
1. **MonoGameHub.Core** - Business logic library
   - Models: `MonoGameProject`, `MonoGameTemplate`, `AppSettings`
   - **Service Interfaces**: `IProjectService`, `INuGetService`, `ITemplateService`, `ISettingsService`
   - **Services Implemented**:
     - `ProjectService` - Full project scanning, analysis, build/run/restore operations
     - `NuGetService` - NuGet API integration with wildcard version resolution
     - `TemplateService` - Template discovery, installation, and management
     - `SettingsService` - Configuration persistence and .NET SDK detection
   - NuGet packages: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite, NuGet.Protocol, DependencyInjection

2. **MonoGameHub.Desktop** - Avalonia UI application
   - MVVM pattern with CommunityToolkit.Mvvm
   - Markdown.Avalonia for content rendering
   - 6-tab interface (Projects, Installs, New Project, Settings, News, Resources)
   - Dark theme with MonoGame branding
   - Header with branding, status bar with version info

3. **MonoGameHub.Tests** - xUnit test project
   - Unit tests for `NuGetService` and `SettingsService`
   - Async/await test support

**Phase 1 Complete - Core Services:**
- ✅ **ProjectService**: Scans folders recursively for MonoGame projects, analyzes `.csproj` files, detects platforms, identifies legacy MGCB vs modern Pipeline, resolves wildcard versions, executes build/run/restore commands
- ✅ **NuGetService**: Queries NuGet.org v3 API, resolves wildcard patterns like `3.8.*` and `3.8.5-develop.*`, retrieves package metadata
- ✅ **TemplateService**: Lists available templates from NuGet, installs/uninstalls via `dotnet new`, detects installed templates, classifies version types
- ✅ **SettingsService**: Persists settings to JSON in AppData, manages environment variables, detects .NET SDK version
- ✅ **Testing**: Unit tests validate NuGet integration and settings persistence
- ✅ **Documentation**: Comprehensive `IMPLEMENTATION.md` with usage examples and architecture decisions

**Build Status:**
- ✅ All projects build successfully with 0 warnings
- ✅ Cross-platform compatibility maintained
- ✅ Core business logic fully functional
- ✅ Async/await with progress reporting throughout
- ✅ Ready for Phase 2 (UI integration with ViewModels)

**Current Capabilities:**
- ✅ Scan and analyze MonoGame projects from file system
- ✅ Query and install MonoGame templates
- ✅ Resolve package versions from NuGet
- ✅ Execute dotnet CLI commands (build, run, restore)
- ✅ Detect .NET SDK version
- ✅ Persist and load application settings

**UI Features Implemented:**
- Tab navigation for all 6 main sections
- New Project form with template selection
- Settings page with theme and IDE preferences
- Placeholder layouts for Projects, Installs, News, and Resources tabs
- Status bar showing MonoGame version and .NET version

### Motivation
- Move the main fishing loop into the backend worker so the UI remains responsive and the loop can be stopped safely.
- Replace console logging with IPC so the frontend receives realtime updates via the `state-update` Tauri event.
- Restore detection by using screen-capture + pixel color counting (red bite / yellow caught) and perform input actions for casting/reeling.
- Ensure thread-safe reads of `SharedState` and stop control via an atomic running flag.

### Description
- Added an atomic `running: Arc<AtomicBool>` to `SharedState` and initialize it in `SharedState::new()`.
- Reworked `start_bot` to accept a `tauri::Window`, set the atomic running flag, and spawn the fishing loop in a background thread using `std::thread::spawn`.
- Implemented screen-capture based detection: added `capture_region`, `count_matching_pixels`, and a small `Color` helper; detection uses `image` + `screenshots` to sample `red_region` and `yellow_region` and sets `bite_detected` / `fish_caught` accordingly.
- Integrated mouse input using `enigo` to perform a left-click when casting and spam-click during reeling.
- Emit session updates to the UI by replacing `println!` with `window.emit("state-update", &session_snapshot)` via `emit_session_update` helper.
- Read configuration values with `state.config.read()` at the start of each loop iteration (then drop the lock) and use `while state.running.load(Ordering::Relaxed)` as the loop condition so `Stop` immediately terminates the thread.
- Updated API and dependencies: changed `start_session` in `src-tauri/src/main.rs` to pass the `Window` to `start_bot`, and added `image`, `screenshots`, and `enigo` to `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`.
- Updated `stop_bot` to set the `running` flag to `false` and mark the session stopped.

### Testing
- No automated tests or CI runs were executed for this change.
- Recommend running `cargo build` for the `src-tauri` crate and project CI to validate compilation and runtime behavior on target platforms.

body: ## Brief summary Add support for importing chapters from .cue files in the audiobook chapters editor, allowing users to easily apply chapter markers from existing cue sheet files. ## Which issue is fixed? https://github.com/advplyr/audiobookshelf/issues/3181 https://github.com/advplyr/audiobookshelf/issues/2863 https://github.com/advplyr/audiobookshelf/issues/2327 ## In-depth Description This PR introduces a new modal component (`ChaptersCueImportModal`) that enables users to import chapter information from standard .cue files. Cue sheets are commonly used to define track/chapter positions in audio files. **Key features:** - **File selection**: Users can select a .cue file via a file picker triggered by the "Import .cue" button on the chapters page - **CUE parsing**: The parser extracts TRACK, TITLE, and INDEX 01 commands, converting MM:SS:FF timecodes (where FF is frames at 75fps) to seconds - **Preview**: Before applying, users can preview all detected chapters with their start times and titles in a scrollable list - **Error handling**: Invalid or empty .cue files display appropriate error messages and disable the apply button - **Integration**: Imported chapters replace existing chapters and automatically calculate end times based on subsequent chapter starts and media duration **Technical details:** - Parses standard CUE sheet format (ignores REM comments, handles quoted and unquoted titles) - Converts frame-based timecodes (75 frames per second) to precise seconds - Falls back to "Track N" naming when titles are missing - Sorts chapters by start time and filters out invalid entries ## How have you tested this? - Added Cypress component tests covering: - Successful import of valid .cue file with multiple tracks - Error handling for empty .cue files - Error handling for malformed timecodes - Error handling for non-.cue content - Manual testing with various .cue files Run tests: `npx cypress run --component --spec "client/cypress/tests/components/pages/ChaptersCueImport.cy.js"` ## Screenshots

## Fix flutter-mobile-build.yml workflow runner issue

### Analysis
The workflow file had issues that prevented it from running when manually triggered:
1. Incorrect syntax in iOS signing condition (line 154)
2. Potential runner availability issues with macOS runners
3. The notify job always requires both android and iOS to complete

### Plan
- [x] Fix syntax error in iOS signing certificate condition (line 154)
- [x] Make iOS job optional/conditional to avoid blocking the workflow
- [x] Update notify job dependencies to handle when iOS job is skipped
- [x] Change iOS build to use --no-codesign instead of requiring signing certificates
- [x] Remove disabled signing step and replace with documentation
- [x] Fix iOS artifact upload path and condition
- [x] Improve artifact naming to clarify it's an unsigned bundle
- [x] Make notify job condition more explicit
- [x] Verify workflow syntax and structure
- [x] Run security checks
- [x] Add IPA generation for AltStore/AltServer compatibility
- [x] Improve provisioning profile UUID extraction
- [x] Fix artifact summary for workflow_dispatch builds
- [x] Complete and ready for manual testing

### Changes Made
1. **Fixed iOS signing certificate condition**: Removed the invalid syntax that tried to check secret existence
2. **Made iOS job conditional**: Only runs on `workflow_dispatch` or release tags
3. **AltStore/AltServer Support**: 
   - Creates unsigned IPA file compatible with AltStore/AltServer
   - IPA is properly packaged (Payload/Runner.app structure)
   - Supports optional signed IPA builds when certificates are configured

4. **Improved provisioning profile handling**: Uses `security cms` and `plutil` instead of grep/sed for robust UUID extraction
5. **Fixed artifact summary**: Now correctly shows iOS IPA artifacts for workflow_dispatch builds

### Result
The workflow can now:
- Be manually triggered via workflow_dispatch
- Generate proper IPA files for AltStore/AltServer installation
- Support both unsigned (default) and signed (optional) iOS builds
- Provide accurate build summaries for all build types

## Summary

Removes the `tabs` permission from the extension to comply with Chrome Web Store policy.

## Chrome Web Store Violation

**Violation ID:** Purple Potassium  
**Issue:** The `tabs` permission is not required for the APIs used by this extension

## Technical Details

The extension only uses:
- `chrome.tabs.query({})` - works without `tabs` permission
- `chrome.tabs.remove()` - works without `tabs` permission
- `chrome.tabs.onCreated` - works without `tabs` permission
- Basic tab properties (`id`) - works without `tabs` permission

The `tabs` permission is only needed when accessing sensitive properties like `url`, `title`, or `favIconUrl`, which this extension does not use.

body:
## Description

ConfigEditor.ps1 exceeded 2500 lines with mixed concerns (UI, validation, save operations). Extracted validation and save logic into dedicated modules following single responsibility principle.

### Changes

**New Modules**
- `scripts/Invoke-ConfigurationValidation.ps1` (177 lines)
  - Platform-specific validation (Steam, Epic, Riot, standalone, direct)
  - Returns structured errors: `@{ Control = 'FieldName'; Key = 'localizationKey' }`
  - Zero dependencies - callable from CLI, tests, build scripts
  
- `gui/ConfigEditor.Save.ps1` (990 lines)
  - All Save-*Data functions consolidated
  - Helper functions: Set-PropertyValue, Protect-Password, Unprotect-Password
  - Calls validation module before persisting

**Modified Files**
- `gui/ConfigEditor.ps1`: Reduced 2560 → 1558 lines (39% reduction)
  - Removed Get-GameValidationErrors, all Save-* functions
  - Added dot-sourcing for validation and save modules
  
- `gui/ConfigEditor.Events.ps1`: Blur validation refactored
  - Validate*OnBlur methods now call Invoke-ConfigurationValidation
  - Removed duplicate regex patterns and Test-Path checks

- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`: Module structure documented

**Code Quality Fixes**
- Added missing Riot platform validation
- Fixed Discord settings path inconsistency (now uses `integrations.discord` consistently)
- Enhanced security: password encryption failures return empty string vs plain text fallback

### Before/After Example

```powershell
# Before: Inline duplicate validation in Events + Save
[void] ValidateSteamAppIdOnBlur() {
    if ($steamAppId -notmatch '^\d{7}$') { /* inline error */ }
}
function Save-CurrentGameData {
    if ($SteamAppId -notmatch '^[0-9]{7}$') { /* duplicate regex */ }
}

# After: Single source of truth
[void] ValidateSteamAppIdOnBlur() {
    $errors = Invoke-ConfigurationValidation -Platform "steam" -SteamAppId $id
    if ($errors) { $this.uiManager.SetInputError(...) }
}
function Save-CurrentGameData {
    $errors = Invoke-ConfigurationValidation -GameId $id -Platform $platform -SteamAppId $appId
    if ($errors.Count -gt 0) { return }
}
```

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Refactoring
- [ ] Other (please describe)

- [x] Tests pass locally

- [x] Manual testing completed

**Validation Module Tests**
- Valid/invalid Game IDs (alphanumeric + hyphen/underscore)
- Steam AppID (7-digit numeric)

----

*This section details on the original issue you should resolve*

<issue_title>Refactor validation logic into modular structure</issue_title>
<issue_description>## Summary

Refactor the validation and save logic from `ConfigEditor.ps1` into separate modules to improve maintainability, testability, and reusability.

## Current Problems

1. **ConfigEditor.ps1 is bloated**: Over 2400 lines mixing initialization, UI, save, and validation logic
2. **Single Responsibility Principle violation**: GUI script directly contains validation logic
3. **Lack of testability**: Validation logic cannot be tested independently
4. **Low reusability**: Validation functions cannot be called from other scripts
5. **Code duplication**: Validation rules duplicated between save-time (`Get-GameValidationErrors`) and blur-time (`Validate*OnBlur` methods)

## Proposed Structure

\`\`\`
gui/
  ConfigEditor.ps1           # Initialization and orchestration (reduced)
  ConfigEditor.Save.ps1      # Save processing aggregation (NEW)
  ConfigEditor.UI.ps1        # Existing
  ConfigEditor.Events.ps1    # Existing (blur validation calls validation module)
  ConfigEditor.State.ps1     # Existing
  ConfigEditor.*.ps1         # Other existing modules

scripts/
  Invoke-ConfigurationValidation.ps1  # Independent validation logic module (NEW)
\`\`\`

## Module Responsibilities

### scripts/Invoke-ConfigurationValidation.ps1 (NEW)

**Purpose**: Centralized validation logic with no dependencies

**Functions**:
- \`Invoke-ConfigurationValidation\`: Main validation entry point
- Platform-specific validation rules (Steam, Epic, Riot, standalone, direct)
- Returns structured error objects: \`@{ Control = 'FieldName'; Key = 'localizationKey' }\`

**Example**:
\`\`\`powershell
\$errors = Invoke-ConfigurationValidation -GameId \$id -Platform \$platform -SteamAppId \$appId
if (\$errors.Count -gt 0) {
    # Handle validation errors
}
\`\`\`

### gui/ConfigEditor.Save.ps1 (NEW)

**Purpose**: Aggregation of all save-related functions

**Functions**:
- \`Save-CurrentGameData\`: Save game configuration
- \`Save-CurrentAppData\`: Save managed application configuration
- \`Save-GlobalSettingsData\`: Save global settings
- \`Save-OBSSettingsData\`: Save OBS integration settings
- \`Save-DiscordSettingsData\`: Save Discord integration settings
- \`Save-VTubeStudioSettingsData\`: Save VTube Studio integration settings

**Dependencies**: Calls \`Invoke-ConfigurationValidation\` for validation

### gui/ConfigEditor.Events.ps1 (MODIFIED)

**Changes**:
- Refactor all \`Validate*OnBlur\` methods to call \`Invoke-ConfigurationValidation\`
- Remove duplicate regex patterns and Test-Path checks
- Keep event handler registration logic

**Before**:
\`\`\`powershell
function ValidateSteamAppIdOnBlur {
    \$steamAppId = \$this.Text.Trim()
    if (\$steamAppId -notmatch '^\d{7}\$') {
        # Inline validation logic (DUPLICATE)
    }
}
\`\`\`

**After**:
\`\`\`powershell
function ValidateSteamAppIdOnBlur {
    \$platform = \$script:Window.FindName("PlatformComboBox").SelectedItem.Tag
    \$steamAppId = \$this.Text.Trim()
    \$errors = Invoke-ConfigurationValidation -Platform \$platform -SteamAppId \$steamAppId
    \$steamError = \$errors | Where-Object { \$_.Control -eq 'SteamAppIdTextBox' }
    if (\$steamError) {
        \$script:UIManager.SetInputError('SteamAppIdTextBox', \$steamError.Key, \$true)
    }
}
\`\`\`

### gui/ConfigEditor.ps1 (MODIFIED)

**Changes**:
- Remove \`Get-GameValidationErrors\` function (moved to Invoke-ConfigurationValidation)
- Remove all \`Save-*Data\` functions (moved to ConfigEditor.Save.ps1)
- Keep initialization and orchestration logic only
- Dot-source the new modules:
  \`\`\`powershell
  . (Join-Path -Path \$appRoot -ChildPath "scripts/Invoke-ConfigurationValidation.ps1")
  . (Join-Path -Path \$appRoot -ChildPath "gui/ConfigEditor.Save.ps1")
  \`\`\`

## Dependency Design

\`\`\`
ConfigEditor.ps1 (Initialization)
  ├→ ConfigEditor.UI.ps1
  ├→ ConfigEditor.Events.ps1 (calls Invoke-ConfigurationValidation for blur validation)
  └→ ConfigEditor.Save.ps1 (calls Invoke-ConfigurationValidation for save-time validation)

scripts/Invoke-ConfigurationValidation.ps1 (Validation logic, no dependencies)
\`\`\`

## Benefits

### 1. Clear Separation of Concerns
- Each module has a single, well-defined responsibility
- Easy to understand what each file does

### 2. Improved Maintainability
- Changes to validation rules only require editing one file
- Editing scope is limited per function

### 3. Enhanced Testability
\`\`\`powershell
Describe "Invoke-ConfigurationValidation" {
    It "Should reject invalid Steam AppID" {
        \$result = Invoke-ConfigurationValidation -GameId "test" -Platform "steam" -SteamAppId "123"
        \$result.Errors | Should -Not -BeNullOrEmpty
    }
}
\`\`\`

### 4. Better Reusability
- Validation logic can be called from CLI tools, build scripts, or API endpoints
- Single source of truth for all validation rules

### 5. ...

</details>

This PR updates [sqlparse](https://pypi.org/project/sqlparse) from **0.4.2** to **0.5.5**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 0.5.5
   ```
   ----------------------------

Bug Fixes

* Fix DoS protection to raise SQLParseError instead of silently returning None
  when grouping limits are exceeded (issue827).
* Fix splitting of BEGIN TRANSACTION statements (issue826).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.5.4
   ```
   ----------------------------

Enhancements

* Add support for Python 3.14.
* Add type annotations to top-level API functions and include py.typed marker
  for PEP 561 compliance, enabling type checking with mypy and other tools
  (issue756).
* Add pre-commit hook support. sqlparse can now be used as a pre-commit hook
  to automatically format SQL files. The CLI now supports multiple files and
  an `--in-place` flag for in-place editing (issue537).
* Add `ATTACH` and `DETACH` to PostgreSQL keywords (pr808).
* Add `INTERSECT` to close keywords in WHERE clause (pr820).
* Support `REGEXP BINARY` comparison operator (pr817).

Bug Fixes

* Add additional protection against denial of service attacks when parsing
  very large lists of tuples. This enhances the existing recursion protections
  with configurable limits for token processing to prevent DoS through
  algorithmic complexity attacks. The new limits (MAX_GROUPING_DEPTH=100,
  MAX_GROUPING_TOKENS=10000) can be adjusted or disabled (by setting to None)
  if needed for legitimate large SQL statements.
* Remove shebang from cli.py and remove executable flag (pr818).
* Fix strip_comments not removing all comments when input contains only
  comments (issue801, pr803 by stropysh).
* Fix splitting statements with IF EXISTS/IF NOT EXISTS inside BEGIN...END
  blocks (issue812).
* Fix splitting on semicolons inside BEGIN...END blocks (issue809).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.5.3
   ```
   ----------------------------

Bug Fixes

* This version introduces a more generalized handling of potential denial of
  service attack (DOS) due to recursion errors for deeply nested statements.
  Brought up and fixed by living180. Thanks a lot!
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.5.2
   ```
   ----------------------------

Bug Fixes

* EXTENSION is now recognized as a keyword (issue785).
* SQL hints are not removed when removing comments (issue262, by skryzh).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.5.1
   ```
   ----------------------------

Enhancements

* New "compact" option for formatter. If set, the formatter tries to produce
  a more compact output by avoiding some line breaks (issue783).

Bug Fixes

* The strip comments filter was a bit greedy and removed too much
  whitespace (issue772).
  Note: In some cases you might want to add `strip_whitespace=True` where you
  previously used just `strip_comments=True`. `strip_comments` did some of the
  work that `strip_whitespace` should do.
* Fix error when splitting statements that contain multiple CASE clauses
  within a BEGIN block (issue784).
* Fix whitespace removal with nested expressions (issue782).
* Fix parsing and formatting of ORDER clauses containing NULLS FIRST or
  NULLS LAST (issue532).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.5.0
   ```
   ----------------------------

Notable Changes

* Drop support for Python 3.5, 3.6, and 3.7.
* Python 3.12 is now supported (pr725, by hugovk).
* IMPORTANT: Fixes a potential denial of service attack (DOS) due to recursion
  error for deeply nested statements. Instead of recursion error a generic
  SQLParseError is raised. See the security advisory for details:
  https://github.com/andialbrecht/sqlparse/security/advisories/GHSA-2m57-hf25-phgg
  The vulnerability was discovered by uriyay-jfrog. Thanks for reporting!

Enhancements

* Splitting statements now allows to remove the semicolon at the end.
  Some database backends love statements without semicolon (issue742).
* Support TypedLiterals in get_parameters (pr749, by Khrol).
* Improve splitting of Transact SQL when using GO keyword (issue762).
* Support for some JSON operators (issue682).
* Improve formatting of statements containing JSON operators (issue542).
* Support for BigQuery and Snowflake keywords (pr699, by griffatrasgo).
* Support parsing of OVER clause (issue701, pr768 by r33s3n6).

Bug Fixes

* Ignore dunder attributes when creating Tokens (issue672).
* Allow operators to precede dollar-quoted strings (issue763).
* Fix parsing of nested order clauses (issue745, pr746 by john-bodley).
* Thread-safe initialization of Lexer class (issue730).
* Classify TRUNCATE as DDL and GRANT/REVOKE as DCL keywords (based on pr719
  by josuc1, thanks for bringing this up!).
* Fix parsing of PRIMARY KEY (issue740).

Other

* Optimize performance of matching function (pr799, by admachainz).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.4.4
   ```
   ----------------------------

Notable Changes

* IMPORTANT: This release fixes a security vulnerability in the
  parser where a regular expression vulnerable to ReDOS (Regular
  Expression Denial of Service) was used. See the security advisory
  for details: https://github.com/andialbrecht/sqlparse/security/advisories/GHSA-rrm6-wvj7-cwh2
  The vulnerability was discovered by erik-krogh from GitHub
  Security Lab (GHSL). Thanks for reporting!

Bug Fixes

* Revert a change from 0.4.0 that changed IN to be a comparison (issue694).
  The primary expectation is that IN is treated as a keyword and not as a
  comparison operator. That also follows the definition of reserved keywords
  for the major SQL syntax definitions.
* Fix regular expressions for string parsing.

Other

* sqlparse now uses pyproject.toml instead of setup.cfg (issue685).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 0.4.3
   ```
   ----------------------------

Enhancements

* Add support for DIV operator (pr664, by chezou).
* Add support for additional SPARK keywords (pr643, by mrmasterplan).
* Avoid tokens copy (pr622, by living180).
* Add REGEXP as a comparision (pr647, by PeterSandwich).
* Add DISTINCTROW keyword for MS Access (issue677).
* Improve parsing of CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (pr662, by chezou).

Bug Fixes

* Fix spelling of INDICATOR keyword (pr653, by ptld).
* Fix formatting error in EXTRACT function (issue562, issue670, pr676, by ecederstrand).
* Fix bad parsing of create table statements that use lower case (issue217, pr642, by mrmasterplan).
* Handle backtick as valid quote char (issue628, pr629, by codenamelxl).
* Allow any unicode character as valid identifier name (issue641).

Other

* Update github actions to test on Python 3.10 as well (pr661, by cclaus).
   ```
   
  
</details>

body:
# Add RHEL 10 Support to CP Ansible (preserve RHEL 9 tests)

## 📋 Summary

This PR introduces **RHEL 10 support** to the Confluent Platform Ansible collection while maintaining backward compatibility with RHEL 9. The distribution follows an **80/20 strategy** where 80% of tests run on RHEL 10 (modern stack) and 20% remain on RHEL 9 (compatibility/legacy features).

### Key Changes
- ✅ **RHEL 10 Support**: 38 scenarios (80.9%) now use `redhat/ubi10-minimal` with Java 21
- ✅ **RHEL 9 Compatibility**: 8 scenarios (19.1%) preserved on `redhat/ubi9-minimal` with Java 17
- ✅ **Dockerfile Optimization**: Leveraged existing `Dockerfile-rhel-java21.j2` instead of creating new ones
- ✅ **Python Dependencies**: Fixed `packaging` module installation for RHEL 10

## 🎯 Distribution Strategy

### RHEL Version Distribution

| **RHEL 9 Scenarios (Java 17 - 19.1%)** | **RHEL 10 Scenarios (Java 21 - 80.9%)** |
|---|---|
| `archive-plain-rhel-fips` | `archive-community-plaintext-rhel` |

## 🛡️ RHEL 9 Feature Coverage

The **8 RHEL 9 scenarios** were strategically selected to ensure comprehensive backward compatibility testing across all major Confluent Platform features:

### 🔐 Authentication Coverage (100%)
| Feature | Scenarios | Coverage |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| **SCRAM** | `rbac-scram-custom-rhel-fips`, `scram-rhel` | SHA-256 & SHA-512 variants |
| **Kerberos** | `kerberos-customcerts-rhel`, `scram-rhel`, `kafka-connect-replicator-plain-kerberos-rhel-fips` | MIT Kerberos server, keytab management |
| **RBAC** | `rbac-scram-custom-rhel-fips`, `rbac-mds-mtls-custom-rhel-fips` | Local & remote MDS |
| **OAuth/OIDC** | `rbac-scram-custom-rhel-fips` | SSO with Azure IdP simulation |

### 🛡️ Security Coverage (87.5%)
| Feature | Scenarios | Coverage |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| **FIPS** | `archive-plain-rhel-fips`, `rbac-scram-custom-rhel-fips`, `rbac-mds-mtls-custom-rhel-fips`, `kafka-connect-replicator-plain-kerberos-rhel-fips` | Federal security standards |
| **mTLS** | `multi-ksql-connect-rhel`, `rbac-mds-mtls-custom-rhel-fips`, `kerberos-customcerts-rhel` | Mutual TLS authentication |
| **Custom Certs** | `rbac-scram-custom-rhel-fips`, `kerberos-customcerts-rhel`, `rbac-mds-mtls-custom-rhel-fips`, `kafka-connect-replicator-plain-kerberos-rhel-fips` | Custom PKI management |

### 📦 Installation Coverage (37.5%)
| Feature | Scenarios | Coverage |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| **Archive Installation** | `archive-plain-rhel-fips` | Tarball-based deployment |
| **Custom Repositories** | `plaintext-rhel-customrepo` | Custom YUM repo configuration |

### 🔗 Component Coverage (100%)
| Feature | Scenarios | Coverage |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| **Multiple KSQL** | `multi-ksql-connect-rhel` | 2 distinct KSQL clusters |
| **Multiple Connect** | `multi-ksql-connect-rhel`, `rbac-scram-custom-rhel-fips` | Up to 3 Connect clusters |
| **Replicator** | `kafka-connect-replicator-plain-kerberos-rhel-fips` | Cross-cluster replication |

### 🏢 Enterprise Coverage (75%)
| Feature | Scenarios | Coverage |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| **MDS/RBAC** | `rbac-scram-custom-rhel-fips`, `rbac-mds-mtls-custom-rhel-fips` | Local & remote MDS |
| **USM Agent** | `scram-rhel`, `kerberos-customcerts-rhel`, `multi-ksql-connect-rhel` | Various auth methods |
| **SSO Integration** | `rbac-scram-custom-rhel-fips` | OIDC authentication |
| **Hub Plugins** | `archive-plain-rhel-fips` | Confluent Hub connector installation |

### ⚙️ Advanced Features (62.5%)
| Feature | Scenarios | Coverage |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| **Log Redaction** | `archive-plain-rhel-fips` | Sensitive data filtering |
| **Multi-cluster** | `rbac-mds-mtls-custom-rhel-fips`, `kafka-connect-replicator-plain-kerberos-rhel-fips` | Cross-cluster operations |
| **Custom Configurations** | `archive-plain-rhel-fips`, `plaintext-rhel-customrepo`, `multi-ksql-connect-rhel` | Advanced customization |

## ⚠️ Important Caveats

### Java Compatibility
- **RHEL 10** ships with **OpenJDK 25** by default, but our tests use **OpenJDK 21** for consistency
- **RHEL 9** scenarios remain on **OpenJDK 17** where explicitly required by Dockerfiles
- **Java 17 is not available** in RHEL 10 repositories, hence scenarios using `Dockerfile-rhel-java17.j2` remain on RHEL 9

### Python Dependencies
- **RHEL 10** includes Python 3.12 by default but lacks the `packaging` module required by Ansible
- Added `packaging` module installation in `roles/common/tasks/redhat.yml` **before** pip upgrade
- This ensures compatibility with Ansible's package management on RHEL 10

### Image Standardization
- **RHEL 10** tests use **only** `redhat/ubi10-minimal` (no AlmaLinux/Rocky Linux flavors)
- **AlmaLinux 10** and **Rocky Linux 10** variants were converted to `ubi10-minimal` for consistency
- This simplifies maintenance while ensuring broad RHEL-family compatibility

## 🔧 Technical Changes

### Files Modified
- **47 `molecule.yml` files** - Updated image and dockerfile references
- **`roles/common/tasks/redhat.yml`** - Added packaging module installation
- **`roles/common/vars/main.yml`** - Added packaging to pip_packages
- **`molecule/certificates.yml`** - Updated Java versions and FIPS support
- **`molecule/Dockerfile-rhel-tar.j2`** - Updated Java version for archive scenarios

## ✅ Testing Strategy

This distribution ensures:
- **Forward Compatibility**: 80% of tests validate RHEL 10 readiness
- **Backward Compatibility**: 20% of tests maintain RHEL 9 support
- **Feature Coverage**: All major CP features tested on both versions
- **Risk Mitigation**: Critical enterprise features validated on stable RHEL 9
 Molecule Run: https://semaphore.ci.confluent.io/workflows/c9d2f70f-a25b-4901-b1ea-e059a5eda524

---

**Note**: This PR maintains full backward compatibility while positioning the project for RHEL 10 adoption. The strategic 80/20 split ensures comprehensive testing coverage while minimizing risk.

author: michareiser
body:
## Summary

ty has good handling for handling CTRL+C during type checking. However, pressing CTRL+C is completely ignored when printing diagnostics. ty happily keeps spamming your terminal until it has printed all diagnostics (how rude of you to interrupt it while doing this important job). This can be especially frustrating if there are many diagnostics.

The reason our CTRL+C handling doesn't work when printing diagnostics is that printing diagnostics happens on the main thread, which is also the one that sets the cancellation flag in the Salsa DB when we receive the CTRL+C signal. That means the CTRL+C signal is queued but processed only after printing all diagnostics. 

We could consider moving diagnostic printing off the main thread but I decided against this because:

* We'll need access to the only `&mut Db` when we start applying fixes. That requires fixes to run on the main thread, and we also want to react to cancellation in that case.
* It would require us to wrap the diagnostic printing in `salsa::Cancelled::catch` which I'm not a huge fan of. 


This is why this PR introduces a new `CancellationToken` that we can use when running expensive operations on the main thread, without relying on Salsa's cancellation mechanism. 

## Test Plan

Tested that pressing Ctrl+C aborts printing diagnostics.
