body:
## Summary

Implements the Mapping API for header aliases, value synonyms, and per-source overrides as specified in PVS-0.3.1.

## Changes

### New Files
- **`packages/api/src/services/mappingService.ts`** (~700 lines)
  - `GlobalMapping`, `AttributeMapping`, `SourceOverride` types
  - CRUD operations at global, attribute, and source levels
  - `getMergedMapping()` with precedence: source > attribute > global
  - `transformRowWithMapping()` for applying mappings to import data
  - `validateAliases()`, `validateValueSynonyms()` helpers

- **`packages/api/src/endpoints/admin/mappings.ts`** (~600 lines)
  - `GET/PUT /admin/settings/mappings` (global)
  - `GET/PUT/DELETE /admin/settings/attributes/{id}/mapping`
  - `GET/PUT/DELETE /admin/settings/attributes/{id}/mapping/sources/{sourceId}`
  - `POST /admin/imports/preview` (test mappings)
  - All handlers include validation and audit event creation

- **`packages/api/test/mappingService.spec.ts`** (18 tests)
  - Validation tests for value synonyms
  - Merge logic tests for precedence rules
  - Transform logic tests for header/value mapping
  - Edge case tests for unicode, whitespace, etc.

- **`docs/lisa/attributes-console-audit/PVS-0.3.1/README.md`**
  - Complete API documentation with examples

### Modified Files
- **`packages/api/src/apiApp.ts`** - Wired all mapping routes

## Firestore Schema

```
settings/
  attribute_mappings/
    global              # GlobalMapping
  attributes/
    keys/{id}/
      mapping           # AttributeMapping with optional sources map
```

## API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/admin/settings/mappings` | Get global mapping |
| PUT | `/admin/settings/mappings` | Update global mapping |
| GET | `/admin/settings/attributes/{id}/mapping` | Get attribute mapping |
| PUT | `/admin/settings/attributes/{id}/mapping` | Update attribute mapping |
| DELETE | `/admin/settings/attributes/{id}/mapping` | Delete attribute mapping |
| GET | `/admin/settings/attributes/{id}/mapping/sources` | List source overrides |
| GET | `/admin/settings/attributes/{id}/mapping/sources/{sourceId}` | Get source override |
| PUT | `/admin/settings/attributes/{id}/mapping/sources/{sourceId}` | Upsert source override |
| DELETE | `/admin/settings/attributes/{id}/mapping/sources/{sourceId}` | Delete source override |
| POST | `/admin/imports/preview` | Test mapping transformation |

## Merge Semantics

All PUT endpoints support `?merge=true` query parameter for additive updates:
- Without merge: replaces entire document
- With merge: merges aliases and synonyms with existing data

## Testing

```bash
# Run unit tests
cd packages/api && npx vitest run test/mappingService.spec.ts

# All 18 tests pass
```

- Builds on PVS-0.3.0 M1 (Audit backend plumbing)
- Next: PVS-0.3.2 (Audit UI implementation)

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/conekta/openapi/security/code-scanning/2](https://github.com/conekta/openapi/security/code-scanning/2)

In general, to fix this issue you explicitly declare minimal `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions either at the workflow root or for the specific job. This overrides any potentially over‑permissive repository/organization defaults and adheres to the principle of least privilege.

For this specific workflow, the safest and simplest fix without changing existing functionality is to add a `permissions:` block granting only read access to repository contents. The `rdme-openapi` job only checks out the repository (`actions/checkout@v3`) and then calls `readmeio/rdme@v8` with an API key secret; it does not create releases, modify issues, or push commits, so `contents: read` is sufficient. We will add `permissions: contents: read` under the `rdme-openapi` job definition, aligned with `runs-on:`. This change is in `.github/workflows/rdme-openapi.yml`, near line 17.

No additional imports or methods are needed; this is purely a YAML configuration change.

This PR standardizes the currency prefix shown in the Create expense amount input.
- If the currency has a real symbol in CURRENCY_LIST (e.g. $, €, £), we render that symbol as the prefix.

body: **Issue #195** **Issue #200** ## Motivation We need to add support for Drupal 10.6, 11.3 and PHP 8.4, 8.5 as well as remove support for Drupal 10.4, 11.1, and PHP 8.1 and update the automated testing grid to test these versions. Also, we currently have a phpunit.xml but only one. We want to update to having a phpunit.9.xml, phpunit.10.xml and phpunit.11.xml`. ## What does this PR do? - [x] Adds support for PHP 8.4, 8.5, Drupal 10.6 and Drupal 11.3 - [x] Removes support for Drupal 10.4, Drupal 11.1 and PHP 8.1 - [x] Adds support for PHPUnit versions 9, 10 and 11 - [x] Adds support for PostgreSQL 18 - [x] Removes support for PostgreSQL 13 - [x] Schedules each test grid to run at 2 am instead of PHPUnit ## Testing ### Manual Testing 1. Checkout this branch locally, open it in VSCode and "Reopen in Container". 2. Confirm that devcontainer builds properly and open the webpage in the browser to confirm versions. Note it is now building Drupal 11.3 and PHP 8.5 3. Check the Automated workflows that they are being run (and passing!) on: - PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 & 8.5 but NOT PHP 8.1. - PostgreSQL 14 & 18 - Drupal 10.5, 10.6, 11.x, 11.2 and 11.3, but NOT Drupal 10.4 or 11.1. 4. Login to the site built by this container and check that it is on the latest version of everything (Drupal 11.3-dev, PHP 8.5.0, PostgreSQL 18.1) at Admin > Reports > Status report 5. Check the README on this branch and confirm the testing grid renders properly with its badges To test whether the phpunit tests using the correct phpunit.xml file: 1. Change the drupal, php and pgsql versions on `.devcontainer.json` and rebuild the container. 2. Check if the phpunit.xml file is being updated locally to the correct version of phpunit. 3. Run the phpunit tests to confirm if they're working correctly.

body:
## Summary

- Add `Fetcher` base class that all site-specific fetchers inherit from
- Move transform functions (`build_db_from_text_internal`, `build_table_from_text`) to `utils.py` to break circular imports
- Add `httpx` and `beautifulsoup4` as core dependencies, PDF processing libs as optional `[pdf]` extras
- Add type hints to all public methods, PDF dependency guards with helpful error messages
- Update `MockFetcher` to inherit from `Fetcher`, add comprehensive test coverage

## What Fetcher Provides

**Base class methods:**
- `request()` - HTTP with retry logic (3 attempts)
- `fetch_and_write_pdf()` - download, convert HTML if needed, validate PDF
- `ocr()` / `do_ocr()` - tesseract processing with concurrent workers
- `transform()` - build SQLite DB from text files
- `check_if_exists()` - deduplication helper
- Directory setup helpers

**Subclasses implement:**
- `fetch_events()` - site-specific scraping logic

## Usage

```python
from clerk import Fetcher

class MySiteFetcher(Fetcher):
    def fetch_events(self) -> None:
        # Site-specific scraping logic
        ...
```

## Summary

When PRs auto-merge quickly (like PR #237), the push event may not trigger CI, leaving code changes undeployed. This was why the Dijkstra avatar fix was in main but never deployed to production.

### Changes
1. Added `workflow_dispatch` trigger to CI workflow
2. Updated all job conditions to run when manually triggered:
   - Backend tests
   - Frontend tests
   - Build & push
   - Deploy
   - Smoke test
   - Close related issues

### Usage
After merging this PR, if a deploy is missed, run:
```bash
gh workflow run ci.yml --repo jeremymatthewwerner/thinkers-chat --ref main
```

- [ ] Verify Dijkstra avatar is on left in production

> <issue_title>Enable RabbitMQ Exporter for Metrics Collection</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Feature Request: Enable RabbitMQ Exporter for Metrics
> 
> ### Current Status
> The `rabbitmq-exporter` service is currently **disabled/commented out** in [docker-compose.infra.yml](docker-compose.infra.yml#L156-L170) because there is no straightforward way to pass RabbitMQ credentials to the official `kbudde/rabbitmq-exporter` image.
> 
> ### Problem
> The exporter requires:
> - `RABBIT_USER` environment variable (currently stored in Docker secret `rabbitmq_user`)
> - `RABBIT_PASSWORD` environment variable (currently stored in Docker secret `rabbitmq_pass`)
> 
> **Challenge**: Docker secrets cannot be directly passed as environment variables without a shell wrapper, but the official rabbitmq-exporter image doesn't easily support this credential injection pattern.
> 
> ### Current Workaround Configuration (Commented Out)
> ```yaml
> rabbitmq-exporter:
>   image: kbudde/rabbitmq-exporter:1.0.0-RC19@sha256:...
>   secrets:
>     - rabbitmq_user
>     - rabbitmq_pass
>   entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
>   command:
>     - |-
>       export RABBIT_USER="$(cat /run/secrets/rabbitmq_user)"
>       export RABBIT_PASSWORD="$(cat /run/secrets/rabbitmq_pass)"
>       export RABBIT_URL=http://messagebus:15672
>       export PUBLISH_PORT=9419
>       export OUTPUT_FORMAT=JSON
>       export LOG_LEVEL=info
>       exec /bin/rabbitmq-exporter
> ```
> 
> ### Why This Matters
> - **Monitoring**: RabbitMQ metrics (queue depth, message rates, connection count) are valuable for observability
> - **Prometheus Integration**: Exporter would integrate with the existing Prometheus monitoring stack
> - **Dashboard**: Enable Grafana dashboards for RabbitMQ health and performance
> 
> ### Possible Solutions
> 1. **Test & validate** the commented-out shell wrapper approach—it may already work
> 2. **Alternative exporter**: Investigate other RabbitMQ exporters that handle credentials differently
> 3. **Custom wrapper image**: Build a lightweight wrapper that injects secrets before starting the exporter
> 4. **Direct Prometheus support**: Use RabbitMQ's built-in Prometheus plugin if available (requires RabbitMQ 3.8+)
> 5. **Environment-based secrets**: Document passing credentials via `.env` file instead of Docker secrets
>

body:
This PR adds the full implementation of the InferenceNode struct to be used in an inference-only configuration with the network. The InferenceNode struct exposes the following methods:

- `pub fn initialize(&mut self, tensor_parallel_size: Option<usize>, gpu_memory_utilization: Option<f64>,) -> Result<()>` - initializes the InferenceNode
- `pub fn inference(&self, request: &InferenceRequest) -> Result<InferenceResponse>` - runs inference for the given request parameters (standard inference/sampling parameters - top p, temperature, max_tokens) 
- `pub fn shutdown(&mut self) -> Result<()` - shuts down the inference node

Also, `python/extension-impl/src/vllm.rs` is moved to `shared/inference/src/vllm.rs`.

There are also two test files provided that test the UpdatableLLMEngine and InferenceNode at top level, along with several unit tests in `node.rs` and `protocol.rs`

The high level plan after this is to integrate this InferenceNode struct into a special type of node in the network infrastructure. We'll need to create a separate `psyche-inference-node` binary for inference-only network setup, wire up P2P message handling, and implement the 'centralized' gateway router node to forward requests from out API endpoint to the network.

To run the tests, use the following commands:

```
nix develop .#dev-python
uv venv

source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install vllm
uv pip install -e python

cargo test -p psyche-inference --features vllm-tests
```

The change streamlines the codebase by removing manual conversion logic and utilizing annotation-driven mapping, improving maintainability and consistency.

**Refactoring: Migration from Converters to Mappers**

* Replaced all usages of legacy converter classes (e.g., `ProjectCreateRequestConverter`, `ProjectCreateResponseConverter`, etc.) in `ProjectController` with new mapper classes (`ProjectCreateMapper`, `ProjectFetchMapper`, `ProjectsListMapper`, `ProjectPatchMapper`, `ProjectsBatchMapper`). This affects dependency injection and all request/response handling in the controller. body: ## About The Pull Request I've compacted the area used for gas tanks to half while preserving most functionality. All the pipe connections to the rest of Atmospherics are still there, at least as far as they were there with the last half-finished PR that ripped out the center pipes. This allows using the rest of the space for the regular mix tank, as well as more construction space that's stripped of everything except air/fire alarms and lighting. Tank floors are rescaled by 4.5 to account for the fact there is 2/9 of the space available to keep the amount of gas constant. Gas tank control consoles are moved to the pumping room. Redone air supply to/waste removal from Atmos. ## Why It's Good For The Game Atmospherics players other than me (I was born in pipe hell, molded by it) tend to just rip out most of the piping roundstart since they take up space that you need to build projects with. This also prevents mistakes from accidentally connecting to something you didn't want, which is a constant problem for new players, made worse by random hidden distro and waste lines under the floor that smart pipes will automatically connect to. Atmos techs have to put their setups somewhere, and usually the odd double 2x9 fusion chamber ends up both taking away a lot of space, as well as irradiate anyone nearby. The construction area lets you ban those dangerous or space-consuming setups to the edge of the department (and irradiate everyone in space!) and still have tons of room for other projects. Waste handling pipes are another huge problem, because you can't really remove them - some atmospherics setups need them, and station scrubbers stop working if Waste pressure gets too high. The new gas tank layout bans those pipes to space where they can't bother you. For instance, if someone decides to mess with the HFR, you tend to be space-limited everywhere else. Your crystallizer setup ends up taking the small area to the north, and then you put a two 9 tile experiment chambers south of the HFR ... and then you're basically done. Building anything in the Incinerator makes Janitor and Assistant lives miserable when they inevitably get irradiated, and the area next to the I-shape with lockers is another great pick to kill your coworkers with - atmos hardsuits for instance don't protect from radiation at all, and neither do security gear. Actually maxing out on atmos tech slots and have all three doing projects simultaneously during downtime usually results in friction due to these space constraints, or people end up abstaining from doing anything in Atmospherics ahead of time because they know how painful it usually is - so maximizing the space they have available is the way to go here. The PR preserves the requirement for basic atmos tech duties like setting up the air mix and waste handling. ## Testing The in-game screenshots are from an earlier revision where small bugs like missing bridge pipes, wrong gas tank flooring, and visible/hidden pipe confusion happened, but they're all fixed in the final version. ## Changelog :cl: map: Rezone/Repipe/Reconstruct pass on MetaStation Atmospherics including more space, more compact gas storage, and less hidden pipes to bother you /:cl: ## Pre-Merge Checklist - [x] You tested this on a local server. - [x] This code did not runtime during testing. - [x] You documented all of your changes.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## What

Fixes the Google Ads connector to properly handle multiple Customer IDs:
1. Accept Customer IDs separated by commas with optional whitespace (e.g., `5365592627, 4859842495`)
2. Fix a type mismatch bug in the customer ID filtering logic

Previously, the validation regex rejected any whitespace, causing users to get the error "The value must match the pattern The customer ID must be 10 digits. Separate multiple customer IDs using commas." even when following the documented instructions.

Additionally, the `CustomerClientFilter` was comparing `record["id"]` (integer) with `config["customer_ids"]` (list of strings), which would cause the filter to never match.

Resolves: https://github.com/airbytehq/oncall/issues/10620

## How

1. **spec.json**: Updated the regex pattern from `^[0-9]{10}(,[0-9]{10})*$` to `^\\s*[0-9]{10}\\s*(\\s*,\\s*[0-9]{10}\\s*)*$` to allow optional whitespace around commas and at string boundaries while still requiring exactly 10 digits per ID.

2. **source.py**: Updated the parsing logic to strip whitespace from each customer ID and filter out empty strings, ensuring clean IDs are passed to downstream components.

3. **components.py**: Fixed type mismatch in `CustomerClientFilter.filter_records()` by converting `record["id"]` to string before comparing with the list of customer IDs.

## Review guide

1. `source_google_ads/spec.json` - Regex pattern change for validation
2. `source_google_ads/source.py` - Parsing logic to strip whitespace
3. `source_google_ads/components.py` - Type conversion fix in filter

**Key review points:**
- Verify the regex correctly validates: `5365592627`, `5365592627,4859842495`, `5365592627, 4859842495`, ` 5365592627 , 4859842495 `
- Verify the parsing produces clean 10-digit IDs without whitespace for downstream use
- Verify the type conversion fix (`str(record["id"])`) is correct given that `customer_client.id` is defined as integer in the schema

## User Impact

Users can now enter multiple Customer IDs with spaces after commas (e.g., `5365592627, 4859842495, 5552699497`) as naturally expected when following the UI instructions. The customer ID filtering will now work correctly when users specify which accounts to sync.

- [x] YES 💚

- Bumped version from `4.1.4-rc.1` to `4.1.5`
- Added changelog entry for the fix

# Remove GraphQL API implementation, keep REST API only

## Summary
This PR removes the entire GraphQL API implementation from the Spring Boot RealWorld example app, leaving only the REST API. The GraphQL implementation used Netflix DGS framework and provided cursor-based pagination, while the REST API uses traditional offset/limit pagination.

**Changes:**
- Removed Netflix DGS GraphQL plugin and dependency from build.gradle
- Deleted all GraphQL datafetchers (Article, Comment, Profile, Tag, Me)
- Deleted all GraphQL mutations (Article, Comment, Relation, User)
- Deleted GraphQL schema (schema.graphqls) and exception handlers
- Removed generateJava task configuration

The REST API already provides equivalent functionality for all operations.

- Fixed GitHub Actions workflow by upgrading deprecated actions (checkout, setup-java, cache) from v2 to v4

author: davidpanderson
body:
Fixed bug in detection of container state at startup.
If container is paused, unpause it rather than restarting.

(Unix) catch quit signals (INT, QUIT, TERM, TSTP) and pause container.
It now works correctly if you ctrl-C the client.

Checkpoint/restart:
Podman has checkpoint/restore commands, using the CRIU library.
Docker has analogous but different commands.

I added code to the wrapper to periodically checkpoint,
and (on startup) to restore a checkpoint if present.
But I was unable to get this to work.

In fact I couldn't get the underlying Podman commands to work.
If I checkpoint a container, run it some more, stop it, then restore,
I always get the unhelpful error message
Error: OCI runtime error: runc: criu failed: type RESTORE errno 0
(Note to self: make sure the Podman features work
before changing the wrapper).

So I gave up.  But that's OK: the only use case is when the
computer is rebooted, which is rare.
On other cases (e.g. exiting the client),
we pause/unpause, and no work is lost.

I left the code in the wrapper, commented out,
in case we figure out the Podman issue.

also: fix warning msgs in the BUDA web interface

body:
### Motivation
- Add a configurable deinterlace option to the burn/transcode pipeline to support source deinterlacing at `30p` or `60p` (or `off`).
- Ensure deinterlace behavior is zsh-compatible and integrates with existing burn modes (`burnin`, `off`, `subtitleTrack`).
- Do not modify MOV/DV passthrough outputs (force deinterlace off for MOV) and surface the effective mode in config logs.
- For 60p, ensure encoded outputs use the higher output FPS where appropriate (MP4/MKV encode paths).

### Description
- Introduced zsh-compatible helpers: `normalize_deinterlace_mode`, `deinterlace_vf_for_mode`, and `deinterlace_output_fps_args_for_mode` to parse/normalize the CLI value and produce filter and output-arg fragments.
- Added `--deinterlace=off|30p|60p` CLI parsing and a `deinterlace_mode` default; normalized the value early (`normalize_deinterlace_mode`).
- Enforced MOV passthrough behavior: if effective container is `mov`, deinterlace is forced to `off` and an `[INFO] Deinterlace ignored for MOV (DV passthrough)` message and run note are emitted.
- Applied deinterlace only for `mp4`/`mkv` encode paths and only when mode != `off`:
  - `burn_mode=burnin`: prepend deinterlace to the burn filtergraph (`-vf "${deint},${vf}"`).
  - `burn_mode=off` (transcode-only): add `-vf "${deint}"` to the transcode command only when enabled.
  - `burn_mode=subtitleTrack`: apply `-vf "${deint}"` on the video stream during muxing (keeps ASS input, maps, and font attach intact).
- For `60p` mode, the helper adds `-r 60000/1001` (via `deinterlace_output_fps_args_for_mode`) and those args are appended to the relevant output/encode command arrays.
- Updated usage/help strings and configuration logging to include the effective deinterlace mode.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.

Part of https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/issues/24815
**Description**
This PR adds a Health field to ApplicationSetStatus that is automatically calculated from the ApplicationSet's conditions. This enables the UI and CLI to display the health status of an ApplicationSet in a consistent manner with Applications.

Currently, ApplicationSets have conditions (ErrorOccurred, ResourcesUpToDate, RolloutProgressing, ParametersGenerated) but no aggregated health status. The UI has to implement its own health calculation logic which leads to inconsistency between UI and any other clients

Here is the health condition table.

```
| Priority     | Condition              | Condition Status | Resulting Health Status |
|--------------|------------------------|------------------|-------------------------|
| 1 (Highest)  | ErrorOccurred          | True             | Degraded                |
| 2            | RolloutProgressing     | True             | Progressing             |
| 3            | ResourcesUpToDate      | True             | Healthy                 |
| 4 (Default)  | None of the above      | —                | Unknown                 |

```

author: ddrcoder
body:
Summary:
`VisitedTable` accounts for a huge portion of `HNSW::search()` for unbatched searches of large indices.

As demonstrated in the benchmarks shown below, the vector-based implementation is much faster for smaller `ntotal` values, but at ~2M and above, it becomes slower, often significantly so. E.g.: At 64M slots, without batching, a workload of 1000 `set()`/`get()`s is >100x slower. Even with batching, this workload is still 3x slower with vectors.

This is a very likely explanation for the poor performance of HNSW in a 2023 USearch blog post (https://www.unum.cloud/blog/2023-11-07-scaling-vector-search-with-intel), which shows the same high throughput below 1M docs, and the same O(n) slowdown as the size grows beyond >2M:

Differential Revision: D89515309

body:
Implements bash-style heredoc syntax for writing multi-line polyglot code inline, eliminating the need for external files or awkward single-line formatting.

## Changes

**Parser (pf_parser.py)**
- Added `_parse_heredoc_syntax()` to detect `<< DELIMITER` patterns with optional output redirection
- Modified `parse_pfyfile_text()` to collect lines between delimiters, preserving indentation
- Fixed `_LANG_BRACKET_RE` with `re.DOTALL` to handle multi-line code blocks
- Enabled polyglot command execution in `_exec_line_fabric()` (was defined but never called)

**Syntax**
```pf
task demo
  shell [lang:python] << EOF
def greet(name):
    print(f"Hello, {name}!")
    
greet("World")
EOF
end

# With output redirection
task to-file
  shell [lang:python] << EOF > output.txt
print("Goes to file")
EOF
end
```

**Features**
- Works with all 40+ supported languages (Python, Node, Go, Rust, Ruby, etc.)
- Supports mixed-case delimiters (EOF, PyEof, PYTHON_CODE)
- Output redirection: `<< DELIM > file.txt`
- Bash heredocs (without `[lang:]`) pass through unchanged

**Documentation**
- Updated pf-runner/README.md with heredoc section and examples
- Added usage example to main README.md
- Changelog entry with feature description

**Tests**
- test_heredoc.pf: Basic functionality across languages
- test_heredoc_comprehensive.pf: Multi-language coverage
- test_heredoc_validation.pf: Edge cases (quotes, whitespace, special chars)
- test_indentation.pf: Indentation preservation
- example_heredoc_from_issue.pf: Issue reference implementation

## Summary

- Increase minimum storage from 20GB to 50GB
- Increase recommended storage from 50GB to 100GB
- Add context about BuildKit's 10GB default cache

## Why

Users with smaller disks have been running out of space during builds. With the persistent BuildKit daemon (#490) now keeping up to 10GB of build cache by default, plus container images and the registry, a single Rails deployment can use 15-20GB. The previous 20GB minimum left no headroom.

## Changes

```diff
-- **Storage**: 20GB minimum, 50GB recommended
+- **Storage**: 50GB minimum, 100GB recommended
```

```diff
-For storage, container images and build caches add up quickly. Base images for
-languages like Ruby or Python are 50-80MB compressed but expand on disk, and
-buildkit caches intermediate build layers aggressively. A Rails deployment can
-easily use 15-20GB between base images, build cache, and the container registry.
-If you're tight on space, you'll see "no space left on device" errors during builds.

+For storage, container images and build caches add up quickly. Base images for
+languages like Ruby or Python are 50-80MB compressed but expand on disk, and
+BuildKit caches intermediate build layers aggressively—keeping up to 10GB by
+default. A single Rails deployment can use 15-20GB between base images, build
+cache, and the container registry. With multiple apps and their version history,
+usage grows from there. Starting with 50GB gives you comfortable headroom; if
+you're tight on space, you'll see "no space left on device" errors during builds.
```

author: jordi1990
body:
This pull request makes adjustments to the control logic for temperature regulation and compressor soft start modes in the `OpenAmberController`. The main focus is on making the system less sensitive to small temperature changes and updating thresholds for compressor frequency modes.

Control logic adjustments:

* Increased the deadband (`DEAD_BAND_DT`) for temperature control from `0.5f` to `1.0f`, making the system less likely to react to small fluctuations around the setpoint.

Compressor soft start logic updates:

* Modified the threshold values in `DetermineSoftStartMode` to require larger temperature deltas before switching to higher compressor frequency modes, reducing the likelihood of starting at a high frequency.

author: schmidtw
body:
Previously, isValid() only recognized base encodings (gzip, deflate, identity) but not compression level variants (gzip+fastest, etc.). This caused encodings like EncodingGzipBestSpeed to be incorrectly marked as invalid.

Additionally, encode() would silently accept unknown variants like "gzip+unknown" and use NoCompression (the zero value from a map miss), which was surprising behavior.

Changes:
- isValid() now recognizes all compression level variants
- encode() now returns ErrUnsupportedEncoding for unknown variants
- decode() remains lenient, accepting unknown variants (compression level is irrelevant for decompression)

This follows Postel's Law: be conservative in what you send (strict encoding), be liberal in what you accept (lenient decoding).

body:
Yahoo Mail restricts mailto URIs to a single "to" recipient. This adds a user preference to split multiple recipients: first in "to", remainder in "cc".

## Changes

- **Settings UI**: Added switch control in About screen with SecureStore persistence (`cartPartnerUseEmailCC`)
- **Email URI builder**: New `buildMailtoUri()` utility with CC mode support, URL encoding, and whitespace/edge case handling
- **Email integrations**: Updated Groups and Message screens to respect preference when generating mailto URIs

## Example

```typescript
// Standard mode (default, useCC=false)
buildMailtoUri('a@x.com,b@x.com', 'Subject', 'Body', false)
// → mailto:?to=a%40x.com%2Cb%40x.com&subject=Subject&body=Body

// CC mode (useCC=true, Yahoo Mail compatible)
buildMailtoUri('a@x.com,b@x.com', 'Subject', 'Body', true)
// → mailto:?to=a%40x.com&cc=b%40x.com&subject=Subject&body=Body
```

Default behavior unchanged; feature opt-in via About > Settings.

author: joshfkon
body:
The delete background was using absolute positioning with top-0/bottom-0 inside a <tr> element, but position:relative doesn't properly establish a containing block on table rows. This caused the delete background to find a larger containing block (the table) and span all rows below.

Fixed by moving the delete background inside the last <td> element which properly supports position:relative as a containing block. Using inset-y-0 with left-full now correctly sizes the delete background to match the single row's height.

## Key Additions

**Repository Context**
- Monorepo structure: 8 packages, TypeScript, pnpm 10.26.0, Vitest 4.x
- Package dependencies: fast-check must build before others can typecheck

**Build Workflow (with timings)**
- Initial setup: `corepack enable pnpm` → `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (~4-20s) → `pnpm --filter fast-check build` (~40s)
- Validation: format (~15s), lint (~15s), typecheck (~20s), test (minutes)

**Critical Build Dependencies**
- TypeCheck requires packages built first (fails with "Cannot find module" otherwise)
- Windows CI: unpack may fail on existing files, use `|| true` workaround
- CI builds need `EXPECT_GITHUB_SHA=true` env var

**Project Structure**
- Complete directory tree with key paths
- Config file purposes (eslint.config.mjs, vitest.config.mjs, tsconfig.*.json)
- CI/CD workflow breakdown (build-status.yml job dependencies, matrix: Node 20/22/24/latest, Ubuntu/macOS/Windows)

**Development Patterns**
- Changesets workflow: `pnpm bump` for versioning (decline for internal packages)
- Code conventions: ES modules, `import type` for types, explicit boundary types
- Build output: dual ESM/CJS with TypeScript <5.7 compatibility layer

**Final Note**
Instructs agent to trust documented commands (all validated via execution) and minimize exploratory searches.

## **User description** ## Summary Implements Epic PM-06: Real-Time & Notifications for the Project Management module. This epic adds comprehensive real-time collaboration features including WebSocket task updates, user presence indicators, real-time Kanban synchronization, notification preferences, in-app notification center, and email digest functionality. ### Stories Implemented | Story | Description | Commits | |-------|-------------|---------| | PM-06.1 | WebSocket Task Updates | Event broadcasting for PM task CRUD | | PM-06.2 | Presence Indicators | Real-time user presence with Redis | | PM-06.3 | Real-Time Kanban | Live Kanban updates with animations | | PM-06.4 | Notification Preferences | User notification settings with quiet hours | | PM-06.5 | In-App Notifications | Notification center with infinite scroll | | PM-06.6 | Email Digest | Scheduled digest emails with BullMQ | ### Key Features **Real-Time Infrastructure:** - WebSocket gateway with room-scoped event broadcasting - Redis-based presence tracking with 5-minute TTL - React Query cache invalidation on WebSocket events - Correlation ID support to filter own actions **Kanban Enhancements:** - Framer Motion animations for task movements - Optimistic updates with rollback on error - Conflict detection with timestamp comparison - Real-time column count updates **Notification System:** - Per-type and per-channel notification preferences - Quiet hours with timezone support - In-app notification center with date grouping - Mark as read/unread with optimistic updates - Daily/weekly email digest with BullMQ scheduling - Unsubscribe via signed JWT tokens ### Technical Changes **Backend (NestJS):** - Extended RealtimeGateway with PM event handlers - New PresenceService with Redis sorted sets - NotificationsModule with preferences, center, and digest services - BullMQ digest queue with timezone-aware scheduling **Frontend (Next.js):** - useRealtimeKanban hook for WebSocket subscriptions - usePresence and useProjectPresence hooks - NotificationCenter with infinite scroll - Notification preferences settings page **Database:** - Extended NotificationPreference model with PM fields - Added quiet hours and digest configuration ### Testing - All TypeScript type checks pass - ESLint validation complete - Pre-commit hooks verified ## Test Plan - [ ] Verify WebSocket events broadcast on task CRUD - body:
### Motivation
- Provide a runnable monorepo scaffold (backend + frontend) for the AI Trading Dashboard with endpoints for NASDAQ/XAU analysis, pattern engine and Claude integrations.
- Surface live ticks from EOD Historical Data for NASDAQ/XAU signals and enrich sentiment analysis with Marketaux news headlines.
- Deliver a modern dark themed Next.js dashboard UI (5 main panels) and simple service stubs so the team can iterate on ML/Claude integrations safely.

### Description
- Backend (FastAPI): added endpoints and routers for `GET /api/health`, `POST /api/run/all`, `POST /api/run/nasdaq`, `POST /api/run/xauusd`, `POST /api/run/pattern-engine`, `POST /api/claude/analyze-patterns`, and `POST /api/claude/analyze-sentiment`.
- Live data & news hooks: implemented `backend/services/data_fetcher.py` with an EODHD WebSocket helper `fetch_latest_price(...)` to obtain latest ticks; added `backend/services/marketaux_service.py` with `fetch_marketaux_headlines(...)` to pull news headlines. Env/config support added in `backend/config.py` and `.env.example` (`MARKETAUX_API_KEY`, `MARKETAUX_BASE_URL`, `EODHD_API_KEY`).
- Service wiring: updated ML service to include live price in reasoning/metrics (`backend/services/ml_service.py`), integrated Marketaux headlines into sentiment payload (`backend/services/sentiment_analyzer.py`), and kept the pattern engine and Claude pattern stubs for UI consumption.
- Frontend (Next.js + Tailwind): scaffolded `frontend/` app router with components for `NasdaqPanel`, `XauusdPanel`, `PatternEnginePanel`, `ClaudePatternPanel`, `SentimentPanel`; added React Query hooks in `frontend/lib/api.ts`, a small Zustand store, global styles, and Tailwind config. Added Dockerfiles, `docker-compose.yml`, `scripts/setup.sh`, and `scripts/test_api.sh` for local setup and endpoint testing. README updated with Quick Start and data source notes.

### Testing
- Dependency install attempted: `pip install -r backend/requirements.txt` was attempted in this environment but failed due to network/proxy restrictions (package index unreachable) — as a result no automated runtime tests were executed here.
- A simple API test script is included at `scripts/test_api.sh` to exercise `GET /api/health` and the analysis endpoints once dependencies and network access are available.
- Basic verification: the code includes `GET /api/health` returning `{ "ok": true }` and the `Run All` flow wiring that composes ML signals, pattern engine and sentiment stubs; these can be validated locally after installing dependencies and setting env vars.
- No other automated tests were run in this environment due to the network restriction.
